b0e29eb0-ab9e-4b68-be1e-f42e6071ba9f.description:
The heart rate trend on the promenade segment, northbound, in the 4:45–5:15/km band agrees with the result of 18 Nov 2026 where the two measure the same thing: heart rate about 135 on 14 Nov (±2 bpm taken as “about”: the model's choice), and at least 5 steady passes. Acceptance criterion 3, on the author's data.

Revised on 19 Nov 2026 (the author's decision): the preliminary analysis counted pace as distance over total time, waits at the crossings (auto-pause) included, which put August–September passes run at 4:02–4:44/km into the band (34 passes, heart rate 149–154). The application measures pace while moving and rejects a pass stopped for more than 10 s, so those passes are not steady passes and the 34 and 149–154 are no longer conditions.
b0e29eb0-ab9e-4b68-be1e-f42e6071ba9f.label: Matches preliminary analysis

b123dc6d-e4bc-46b0-b2c2-af5f46cada59.label: Steady pass accepted

b1707f8d-4ee5-434c-a5c1-8545b9b1c76a.action: style the components only through the theme's design tokens (the CSS custom properties of the light and dark theme), with 0 colours set outside them

b1707f8d-4ee5-434c-a5c1-8545b9b1c76a.rationale: The application has no component library (ADR Built with React, revised 19 Nov 2026): its own components are styled through its theme, so the theme is the one place a colour changes, in both the light and the dark theme.

b277147e-4dc1-40fe-8a58-9004d82b2740.action: keep in the shared kernel only types and contracts used by at least two parts, with no dependency on a part and no third-party library beyond the allowed pure ones, at most 5% of the source lines, and changes approved by the owners of every part that uses it as the Code review and branching pack decides ownership
b277147e-4dc1-40fe-8a58-9004d82b2740.label: Shared kernel stays small
b277147e-4dc1-40fe-8a58-9004d82b2740.rationale: A shared kernel is shared on purpose and kept small; a growing "common" folder couples everything to everything (Evans, Domain-Driven Design, Shared Kernel).

b2ecee7e-c463-4adf-9bdc-167842a010a9.when: two rules are computed together, the fastest 2 minutes of every run and the easy runs whole by their maximum, then the easy rule alone

b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.description: Speed variation (the coefficient-of-variation condition) is judged on the moving samples, and time spent standing is its own condition: samples below 0.5 m/s plus the gaps where the watch recorded nothing (auto-pause), at most 10 s. Found while comparing with the preliminary analysis of 18 Nov 2026: several August–September promenade passes held 55–110 s of auto-pause at crossings.
b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.gherkin: And a block with a stop in its last 2 minutes is accepted the same way, every metric included

b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.action: remove the definition and its detected instances, and propose it again as a suggestion when it came from one
b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.label: Deletable block
b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.rationale: The runner asked for a way to remove blocks: "nie mam opcji usuwania blokow". The need says nothing more, so the rest is the model's choice: a confirmation first, because the deletion also removes the detected instances (it keeps Analysis and A/B free of a block that no longer exists); a block that came from a suggestion is suggested again, so a deletion by mistake is undone by accepting it again.

b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.action: show in its statistics the trend of each metric shown as its change per 10 minutes, and the decoupling of pace from heart rate over the stretch
b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.label: Trend of a selection
b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.rationale: The runner asked: "linie tredu ?", then: "zrob 1,2 i 3". The model's choices: a trend only within a selection and as a number, not a line over the whole run, where intervals and warm-ups make a straight line misleading; the trend is the least-squares slope of the 10 s windows with movement, given per 10 minutes, for a selection of 1 minute or more; the decoupling (Pa:HR) compares the efficiency, speed per heartbeat, of the stretch's first half with its second, in % (positive: the heart rate drifted up against the pace), as it is reckoned in endurance training (Friel, The Cyclist's Training Bible / TrainingPeaks).
b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.trigger: the runner selects a stretch of a run

b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.given: 10 s windows alternating 140 and 160 bpm, with a stop of 3 windows in the middle
b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.label: Rolling mean of a line
b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.then: the smoothed values are 150 bpm away from the stop, the stop stays a break; the span is 60 s for 30 minutes, 10 s (no smoothing) for 5 minutes, and at most 120 s
b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.when: they are smoothed over 1 minute, and the span is reckoned for a run of 30 minutes and of 5 minutes shown

b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.action: draw each line as the rolling mean of its 10 s windows over a span that grows with the range shown, keeping the breaks at stops
b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.label: Smoothing that follows the zoom
b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.precondition: the run chart is set to Smooth
b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.rationale: The runner asked: "jakiegos spline aby odszumic", then: "zrob 1,2 i 3". The model's choices: a spline only joins points smoothly, a mean removes the noise; the span is 1/30 of the range shown, from 10 s (the windows as they are) up to 2 min; Smooth is the default and Raw / Smooth sits in the chart menu.

b90202ab-2fcb-414f-83ca-2f368c7e56ed.description:
Playwright runs the journeys against the static export served by a plain static file server (scripts/static-server.mjs), with no retries and forbidOnly; scripts/test-metrics.mjs reads the Playwright report and records failed and skipped tests, and npm run check exits non-zero on either. Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026): there is no merge; a change is committed after npm run check passes.

Threshold: all end-to-end tests pass before a change is committed, with 0 skipped

Tool: Playwright (JSON report) with scripts/test-metrics.mjs
b90202ab-2fcb-414f-83ca-2f368c7e56ed.label: Journeys gate the release

c647f82f-e4f1-4c37-b71e-08a72a967714.label: Effort blocks on any route
c647f82f-e4f1-4c37-b71e-08a72a967714.rationale: The author's choice (19 Nov 2026): logical blocks independent of the route, e.g. a time trial on 2 different routes. The model's choice: the 15% margin over the rest of the run (on the author's runs 8% caught every faster finish and interval set), the standard lengths 3, 5 and 10 km and 10, 20 and 30 minutes (1 km caught mostly intervals; it can still be defined from a selection), and the 3 runs.

c6d5b5bc-63e5-4e1d-b3e0-9f4b74617881.description: Everything on one screen, across its whole width (no scrolling at 1440 × 900 and larger). Head: title (or date), date and time, then one compact line of figures (distance, moving time, average pace, average heart rate, elevation gain), device, laps, temperature, "Add to Analysis". Over the chart a strip of laps, one horizontal bar each, a button as wide as the lap on the x axis, named "Lap N · X km" when wide enough: a click selects the lap and zooms to it. Below the head, one card: a toolbar in two rows: the metric pills to choose (up to 4 on, each with its colour swatch); then a short line of what the chart is set to (Bands or Overlaid, by time or distance, blocks drawn) and, at the right end, the "Chart" button (the range shown is announced to screen readers only); the mouse wheel over the chart zooms around the pointer. The "Chart" button slides a menu in from the right, over the map and laps and without dimming the chart: Lines "Bands / Overlaid", Line "Smooth / Raw" (the rolling mean over 1/30 of the range shown, or the 10 s windows), X axis "Time / Distance", Blocks in this run ("Draw on the chart", the list: pointing at one draws it, a click selects it), Make a block (the block types for the selection, or a hint to select first, and "Block from these laps"), Zones (which metrics shown have zones, a link to Settings); it closes with ✕, Escape or the button; a selection (dragged, on the map, a lap: list, label, double click or table row, a block) zooms the chart and the map to it at once; under it, side by side, the chart on the left and on its right the route map (the wheel zooms around the pointer, a drag pans, and the chart then shows the range of time of the route in view; click two points to select) with the run's laps under it, scrolled inside (a click on a lap selects it). The chart: the chosen metrics laid over each other, each line scaled to its own range, the focused metric's ticks at the left, laps as alternating bands, kept blocks as washed bands with names only when the toggle "Blocks" in the toolbar is on (off by default) or for the one block pointed at in the list, zones as stripes, the selection as an accent wash, a crosshair with a tooltip listing every line's value and zone at the pointer; two x axes under it, the chosen one (clock or km) and the other at the same places; the focused metric's average as a dashed line and its min and max as points with their values (from the statistics; a Min, Avg or Max cell pointed at lights its mark); a legend of the lines, each with its range, a click focuses one; an overview strip of the whole run whose window is the range shown, growing and shrinking with the zoom, the selection marked under it: dragging the window moves the range and the selection with it, dragging elsewhere selects a new stretch; the chart takes the height the screen leaves. Drag on the chart to select a stretch; pinch or Ctrl/⌘ + scroll zooms around the pointer, a sideways scroll moves. At the bottom, across the full width: the statistics of the selection (or the whole run, or the zoomed range): its time and distance, the selection told once in its head ("Selection", its clock range, time and distance) and its ✕, which clears it and shows the whole run, a Pa:HR chip (the decoupling of pace from heart rate) for a selection, and a table with a column per metric shown and min, avg and max in rows, and for a selection a row "Trend /10 min".

cdb3ba69-24a7-48b5-a970-522185fa982b.decision: Keep data as files in the runner's folder: columnar JSON (one array per field), user/ separate from derived/, denormalized index files for analysis.

cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.action: reject it for every metric with the reason, so that no metric is left out of an instance on its own
cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.label: Minimum block length
cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.rationale: A fragment shorter than a minute gives no meaningful mean of any metric. One decision per run (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026, need "Strideprism MVP specification": "Never exclude for HR"): an accepted instance counts for every metric, heart rate included, computed from the block's heart rate window. The spec's per-metric minimum (4 minutes for heart rate) is dropped by that decision; the 60 s of the gait metrics becomes the block's minimum.
cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.unwanted_condition: a block instance is shorter than 60 s

cf881669-ade1-4276-8e27-b57217debcd7.action: conform to WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page, with 0 serious or critical automated accessibility violations, every function operable by keyboard alone, and a manual audit with a screen reader before each major release
cf881669-ade1-4276-8e27-b57217debcd7.label: Accessible to WCAG 2.2 AA
cf881669-ade1-4276-8e27-b57217debcd7.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA is the level EN 301 549, the European Accessibility Act and most public-sector rules require; automated checks find only part of the failures, hence the keyboard journey and the manual audit (W3C WCAG 2.2; EN 301 549).

d00107b1-a4df-4790-b933-7c13969f8952.rationale: The runner's remodelling: "4.2 system wybiera mi wszystkie segmenty i je uzywa", and the earlier form of an answer, "tabela wyników z linkami do biegów" with "ranking kolejnych". Showing what was left out and why keeps the result transparent, as for every block (requirement "Result transparency").

d3c81008-1d9a-459b-b77c-ba4b66820d00.action: run only framework and build-tool majors under support, moving off each at least 180 days before its end of support

d3c81008-1d9a-459b-b77c-ba4b66820d00.rationale: Front-end frameworks support a major for a limited time (Angular 18 months, Node.js-based tooling with its runtime); after that, security fixes stop (endoflife.date).

d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.alternatives:
1. A frozen baseline with a ratchet: adoptable today on an old codebase, at the cost of carrying known violations.
2. Warnings only: visible, and ignored within weeks.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.consequences:
• A violation never reaches main, so nobody comes to depend on one.
• Switching the check on needs a clean codebase first; on an old one that is a project of its own.
• A rule that turns out wrong blocks everyone until it is changed, which keeps the rules honest.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.context: The code in this element is cut into parts (modules, packages, libraries) and keeps changing. Without written and checked rules, every shortcut adds a dependency nobody decided on: one module reads another's internals, two packages import each other, and a "common" folder grows until every change touches everything. The forces: rules kept only in a wiki erode within months; a cycle makes two parts one, so neither can be tested, owned or released alone; sharing code saves typing but couples the teams that share it; a boundary nobody owns is crossed by whoever is in a hurry; and an old codebase cannot fix every violation at once. What the parts are (layers, rings, slices) is the Architecture style pack; who owns each part is the Code review and branching pack; this pack keeps the boundaries between the parts.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.decision: The dependency check (scripts/boundaries.mjs) runs in every check of a change (npm run check) and in the unit tests, and any violation fails it: there is no baseline and no exception list. Existing violations were fixed before the check was switched on (19 Nov 2026: the cycles between ingest, prepare, blocks and context were broken by the shared kernel and the pipeline part). Local only for now: a change is committed after npm run check passes.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.label: Every violation fails the build

da832a20-4c6e-48e6-9bce-d34a6396158a.rationale: Declaring each dependency makes it a decision visible in review; rules that are not checked erode with every shortcut (Building Evolutionary Architectures, ch. 2; Spring Modulith, allowed dependencies).

db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.alternatives:
1. A testing trophy: mostly integration tests, better for glue code, slower feedback.
2. An ice-cream cone of manual and end-to-end tests: slow, brittle and late; the shape to move away from.
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.consequences:
• Fast, precise feedback: a failing unit test names the rule that broke.
• Refactoring that changes internal interfaces rewrites many unit tests; test behaviour, not methods, to limit it.
• Wiring bugs (configuration, queries, serialisation) are caught only by the thinner integration layer.
• Requires code where the logic can be called without infrastructure.
• The gate costs build time in proportion to what it proves: coverage is free, a mutation score adds minutes.
• Where the end-to-end tests run decides what they can stop: before the merge, before production, or only after.
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.context: Code lives in this element and changes every week; the tests decide whether a change can be released with confidence or only with hope. The forces: fast tests give feedback in minutes but exercise little of the wiring, while end-to-end tests exercise everything but are slow, brittle and late; coverage shows what was run, not what was checked; tests that share data or depend on order fail at random, and a suite that fails at random is soon ignored; copies of production data make realistic tests but carry personal data; and a test that fails only sometimes teaches everyone to rerun until green. Contract tests between the system's parts and with outside callers are decided in the Communication style and API evolution packs.
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.decision: Tests follow the pyramid, adapted to real data: unit tests of the domain logic under tests/unit run with Vitest on synthetic data, without network access, in under 100 ms each, at least 40% of all tests; integration tests under tests/integration run the processing pipeline against a temporary data folder with the versioned synthetic FIT fixtures (tests/fixtures) and the author's FIT files (test_data, kept out of the repository); a few end-to-end tests, at most 15%, cover import, block-definition, trend, ab-comparison (Playwright, Chromium) against the static export. Every check of a change (npm run check) runs unit and integration tests within 10 minutes, in random order. Gate: coverage of new code, 80%; mutation testing with Stryker is deferred. Flaky tests: quarantine (quarantine.json, nightly run), then a fix or deletion. Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026).
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.label: A test pyramid

The choices and the numbers it is held to must be written down and checked, not rediscovered after users complain. The checks assume one front end per repository with its package.json at the root, a versions.txt listing the endoflife.date products and cycles in use, server templates (htmx) under templates/ or src/, and a RUM table rum_events(name, value, page_group, received_at) fed by the page.

ef4fb321-3d4b-495d-bcb5-7212a4433066.quote: The code in this element must stay easy to understand, test and change as it grows and as people come and go. That needs parts with clear boundaries: a change to one part should not ripple through the others, each part should be testable on its own, and the rules about what may depend on what should hold because the build checks them, not because everyone remembers them. The checks below share one layout: each part lives in src/modules/<name> with its published API in src/modules/<name>/index.ts and its declarations in src/modules/<name>/module.json; shared code, where allowed, lives in src/shared-kernel; the rules are in .dependency-cruiser.cjs and run as `npm run check:deps` (depcruise src --config .dependency-cruiser.cjs); known violations, where frozen, are in .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json.

226353bd-e1a4-4d07-b2db-bf1aecd05a15.description:
Success criterion of step 1: the tool detects at least one change in the author's running that is larger than the noise. Measured automatically on every check (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026, replacing a manual review every 6 weeks): an integration test imports the author's runs, accepts every suggested block, computes the trend of every metric for each, and counts the trends whose verdict is "change" (the fitted change larger than the noise threshold, its 95% interval clear of zero, at least 5 instances). The random-split negative test (at least 9 of 10 random splits without a change) guards against a rule that finds changes everywhere.

Threshold: at least 1 trend with the verdict "change" in the author's runs

Tool: Vitest (tests/integration/acceptance.test.ts) on the author's FIT files

Metric pills, Raw | Corrected, Join points, Trend line and Pace curve switches. One Over time chart per metric on a shared time axis: each block's segments as points in the item's colour and shape, its trend line and noise band, each run's average as one point. With Pace curve on, a Pace curve chart: for each length of time (30 s … 2 h, logarithmic) the fastest stretch of that length inside the item's segments, one line per item, the estimate dashed, each best's gap to it, the estimate read under the pointer, and a note with the predicted times and the critical speed. The table of changes: one row per block (its kind, start and heart rate window as chips, Compare A/B for a kept one), one cell per metric (the change, its percentage, the verdict chip, the noise and the count of segments). The verdicts in words per block. Segments: the segments of a block (choice of block and metric), by date or best or worst first with top N, how many are in and left out with the reasons, each with Open run → (the stretch selected on the run).

27bfbb75-0d7b-42a4-abeb-12bbcbb68e50.alternatives:
1. A regression line through the bests (built first): describes the typical level, but leaves the strongest bests above the estimate and lets easy long runs pull the predictions down.
2. The critical speed model alone, drawn over the axis: a clean two-parameter fit, but it predicts the critical speed held forever, so it overstates every effort beyond about 20 minutes.
3. A three-parameter critical power model (Morton 1996) or the Péronnet–Thibault model: closer to physiology, but ill-conditioned with a handful of uneven bests.
4. A fixed Riegel exponent of 1.06 through the single best stretch: no fit needed, but the runner's own endurance (or the lack of a hard long run) is what the curve should show.
27bfbb75-0d7b-42a4-abeb-12bbcbb68e50.consequences:
• The estimate is the potential the bests imply, not the typical level; it never lies below a measured best.
• An easy long run still steepens the slope (a higher exponent), and the exponent is shown, so a strange fit is visible (1.06–1.08 for trained runners; higher means the long bests were not hard).
• Predicted times follow the envelope: fair for 5 km to the marathon from a strong 10 km, and optimistic for the marathon without hard long runs.
27bfbb75-0d7b-42a4-abeb-12bbcbb68e50.context: The runner wants an estimated pace curve "bazujac na researchu" beside the measured one (the fastest stretch of each length across the runs). The curve must be computed from a few best efforts of uneven quality (an easy long run is the only effort of its length), on the computer, deterministically.
27bfbb75-0d7b-42a4-abeb-12bbcbb68e50.decision: Two models from the literature, fitted to the item's own best stretches: (1) Riegel's power law (Riegel 1981, Athletic records and human endurance): time ∝ distance^b, so speed ∝ time^(−k); the exponent k is fitted by ordinary least squares in log–log to the bests of 3 minutes and more, and the level is then raised to the strongest best, so the line is an envelope no measured best lies above — the law describes a maximal effort, and an easy long run is no such effort (the runner's choice, after seeing bests above a regression line). It is drawn dashed over the whole axis and gives the predicted times of 5 km, 10 km, the half and the marathon. (2) The critical speed model (Monod & Scherrer 1965; Hill 1993; Jones & Vanhatalo 2017, Sports Medicine): distance = CS·t + D′ fitted to the bests of 2–20 minutes, the range the review gives for its validity, reported as the critical speed and D′ in the note, not drawn. At least 3 bests for either fit.
27bfbb75-0d7b-42a4-abeb-12bbcbb68e50.label: Pace curve models

2f20802d-6d6a-4eac-9620-f016383fc5be.rationale: COROS FIT files carry no workout name; asked where the title to filter by ("wybieram tytlu coros test") comes from, the runner chose "Nowe pole „tytuł” biegu: Dowolny tekst nadawany biegowi na ekranie Runs; kryterium = fragment tytułu".

2f223517-a575-43e4-bac5-c331d15faa41.description: One run read from one FIT file. Key: start time. Holds source file, device, distance and duration; owns its samples, laps and 10 s windows. Raw and immutable.
2f223517-a575-43e4-bac5-c331d15faa41.label: Run

2f46f997-ec74-405b-917b-2d3c97b3be0f.description:
The application has no component library: its components are styled through its own theme, the CSS custom properties (tokens) of app/globals.css for the light and dark theme. A unit test (tests/unit/styles.test.ts) refuses a colour set anywhere but in a token: a colour literal in a CSS declaration that is not a custom property, or in a component.

Threshold: 0 colours set outside the theme's tokens

Tool: Vitest over app/globals.css and the components
2f46f997-ec74-405b-917b-2d3c97b3be0f.label: No library internals styled

3120690b-ce09-4693-bbb1-2eafbc8a99ce.given: only 2 imported workouts with the same structure
3120690b-ce09-4693-bbb1-2eafbc8a99ce.label: Two workouts not enough
3120690b-ce09-4693-bbb1-2eafbc8a99ce.then: no workout structure Block Definition is proposed for them

3151aa14-7b07-4207-a5e3-939b1c23c899.alternatives: Desktop app; local server with a database.
3151aa14-7b07-4207-a5e3-939b1c23c899.consequences: Data never leaves the computer; can be published as a plain web page; all processing must fit in the browser.
3151aa14-7b07-4207-a5e3-939b1c23c899.context: One runner, own data, locally; no accounts or hosting in the MVP.
3151aa14-7b07-4207-a5e3-939b1c23c899.decision: Build Strideprism as a Next.js static export (React, TypeScript) that runs entirely in the browser, with no server and no database.
3151aa14-7b07-4207-a5e3-939b1c23c899.label: Static browser-only app

316c4249-8e1b-4104-87de-f1cac5064fa7.description: “Recompute everything” over about 300 runs (the author's data since 3 Aug 2026) finishes within 15 minutes. Threshold from the user's answer: ≤15 min in total.
316c4249-8e1b-4104-87de-f1cac5064fa7.label: Recompute time

318c99a5-6ed7-45ae-98f1-d7daa3f364c2.action: mark the instance as rejected and record the reason for rejection
318c99a5-6ed7-45ae-98f1-d7daa3f364c2.label: Reject with reason
318c99a5-6ed7-45ae-98f1-d7daa3f364c2.rationale: BlockInstance status: accepted, or rejected with reason; needed for transparency (F14).
318c99a5-6ed7-45ae-98f1-d7daa3f364c2.unwanted_condition: an instance fails a matching condition

31df2b33-7d61-4128-bd2a-a8fd73481b33.description: 10 s windows with metric means and quality flags; route segments from GPS tracks.
31df2b33-7d61-4128-bd2a-a8fd73481b33.label: Prepare

31ec5c9f-dc19-4487-a84b-67fbd381ead5.action: show the recomputed trend or A/B comparison, including its bootstrap uncertainty interval, within 3 s
31ec5c9f-dc19-4487-a84b-67fbd381ead5.label: Analysis time budget
31ec5c9f-dc19-4487-a84b-67fbd381ead5.rationale: User's answer on the time budget for the analysis screens.
31ec5c9f-dc19-4487-a84b-67fbd381ead5.trigger: the user changes the metric, context filter or splitting field of a trend or an A/B comparison

31edf6a9-090b-4580-abac-a4c0c13d251f.action: open the run the point comes from, with the block's segment or the curve's stretch selected on it
31edf6a9-090b-4580-abac-a4c0c13d251f.label: Run opened from a point
31edf6a9-090b-4580-abac-a4c0c13d251f.rationale: The runner asked: "po kliknieciu na pubkt chce miec mozliwosc otwarcia biegu". The model's choices: the segment opens selected, so it can be read and made a block at once; the tooltip says a click opens the run and the pointer turns into a hand over a point; a run added whole opens with nothing selected.
31edf6a9-090b-4580-abac-a4c0c13d251f.trigger: the user clicks a point of an Over time chart or of the pace curve on the Analysis screen

Gear: a timeline (Gantt-like) of shoes and heart rate sensors with draggable date-range bars, plus a list with name, type and dates; "Add gear" opens an inline form; changing a range shows how many runs will be reassigned. Tags: editable dictionaries of workout types and technique cues as chips with counts.

338e617d-2563-4e79-997a-bf7596ac10aa.description: Centered onboarding card on a calm background that follows the OS theme (light or dark). First launch: the Strideprism mark, one sentence on what it does, a primary "Choose data folder" button (showDirectoryPicker) and a note that data never leaves the computer. Later launch: the remembered folder name with a "Continue with my-folder" button that confirms access, and a quiet "Choose another folder" link. In Firefox or Safari the card shows only a not-supported message naming Chrome, Edge and Opera, with no buttons.
338e617d-2563-4e79-997a-bf7596ac10aa.label: Welcome

342343ef-917c-4171-99f8-14183dcb563e.gherkin: And after "Recompute everything" it is still not proposed
342343ef-917c-4171-99f8-14183dcb563e.given: the user rejected the recommended route segment Block Definition for the promenade southbound
342343ef-917c-4171-99f8-14183dcb563e.label: Rejected stays rejected
342343ef-917c-4171-99f8-14183dcb563e.then: the promenade southbound is not proposed again
342343ef-917c-4171-99f8-14183dcb563e.when: the user imports 5 new Runs that pass the promenade southbound and detection runs

3427be02-d02e-446f-ab48-68ebfcc2c505.description: First launch: no folder handle is remembered.
3427be02-d02e-446f-ab48-68ebfcc2c505.entry: ask the user to pick the data folder
3427be02-d02e-446f-ab48-68ebfcc2c505.label: Not Chosen

3479a61f-e20a-4dbc-a02d-afa8af07998e.description: Coefficient of variation of speed below 0.15 by default.
3479a61f-e20a-4dbc-a02d-afa8af07998e.label: Check pace steadiness

3569f747-de49-4feb-a212-3644eee53446.action: space the chart by the chosen one and show two x axes: the chosen one, and the other at the same places
3569f747-de49-4feb-a212-3644eee53446.label: Time or distance on the x axis
3569f747-de49-4feb-a212-3644eee53446.rationale: The runner asked: "dodaktowo chce 2 osie x ... czas lub dystans". The model's choices: a toggle "Time / Distance" in the chart's toolbar, remembered in the browser; time by default; the chosen axis has round ticks (a clock, or km), the second axis under it gives the distance at each time tick or the time at each distance tick; the overview strip follows the choice; a stop takes no width when spaced by distance; selection, laps, zoom and the map work the same in both.
3569f747-de49-4feb-a212-3644eee53446.trigger: the runner chooses time or distance for the x axis of the run chart

35cf3a74-f6aa-4e4e-9d29-09e491acb525.action: keep them as the zones of that metric in the data folder, for the run chart to colour
35cf3a74-f6aa-4e4e-9d29-09e491acb525.label: Metric zones in settings
35cf3a74-f6aa-4e4e-9d29-09e491acb525.rationale: The runner asked: "w settingsach chce podawac zakresy", then: "dodaj domyslne strefy ... do testow". The model's choices: a Settings screen in the navigation; any metric of a run can have zones; the runner gives the boundaries between zones (pace as m:ss per km), the zones are named Z1, the easiest, to Zn; heart rate zones can be filled from the maximum heart rate at 60, 70, 80 and 90 % of it; the zones are kept in user/settings.json of the data folder, like the runner's other files; until that file is saved, default zones apply (heart rate 114, 133, 152, 171 bpm; pace 6:00, 5:15, 4:45, 4:15 /km; cadence 160, 170, 180 spm), and a button fills them in again.
35cf3a74-f6aa-4e4e-9d29-09e491acb525.trigger: the runner enters the ranges of a metric on the Settings screen

36038f78-a505-4196-a7a7-9dbac6a637e8.action: keep the JavaScript a route loads before it is interactive within 200 KB compressed, loading the rest on demand
36038f78-a505-4196-a7a7-9dbac6a637e8.label: JavaScript within budget
36038f78-a505-4196-a7a7-9dbac6a637e8.rationale: JavaScript is the costliest byte on a phone: it is downloaded, parsed and run on the main thread, which is what INP measures (web.dev, Performance budgets 101).

3614e7f4-9407-407b-a23b-56e0b424d992.description: A specific fragment of a specific run that meets a definition: start, end, metric means, per-minute profile, the four context layers (the block itself, what came before, the run, the day) and a status: accepted, or rejected with the reason. Derived.
3614e7f4-9407-407b-a23b-56e0b424d992.label: Block Instance

368d77bf-f7ca-4698-8943-e0f8518b648a.action: work in the last 2 versions of Chrome, Edge and Opera (the browsers with the File System Access API), with the main journeys tested in Chromium on every pull request and 0 unsupported language or web features shipped without a polyfill
368d77bf-f7ca-4698-8943-e0f8518b648a.label: Supported browsers work
368d77bf-f7ca-4698-8943-e0f8518b648a.rationale: The user's choice: only Chrome, Edge and Opera are supported; other browsers get a not-supported message. "Last 2 versions" and "0 features without a polyfill" are the Frontend stack pack's thresholds (the model's decision). An explicit browser list lets the build ship only the transpilation and polyfills needed, and the lint catch a feature the list does not have (Browserslist).

37bd5634-0cac-4407-a824-5dfccb39f1a5.description: The user takes a recommended definition in the picker of the Analysis screen.
37bd5634-0cac-4407-a824-5dfccb39f1a5.label: RecommendationAccepted

37de8939-dd70-4e96-827e-5901e301a79b.given: a run of 30 minutes at 6:00/km with 10 minutes at 4:00/km in its middle
37de8939-dd70-4e96-827e-5901e301a79b.label: Pace curve inside the segments
37de8939-dd70-4e96-827e-5901e301a79b.then: over the whole run every length up to 10 minutes is at 4:00, 15 minutes at 4:30 and 30 minutes at about 5:09, with no length beyond the run; inside the first 10 minutes the pace is 6:00 and nothing is longer than the stretch; of two segments the faster counts; across runs each length keeps its faster point
37de8939-dd70-4e96-827e-5901e301a79b.when: the fastest stretch of each length is taken over the whole run, inside its first 10 minutes only, and inside two segments; and the points of two runs are merged

39491f93-4fcc-4f9c-960b-e12750deef8f.description: The six screens plus welcome, instance panel and command palette, on the browser's main thread; computes trends and A/B comparisons from the index files. Served as plain static files.
39491f93-4fcc-4f9c-960b-e12750deef8f.label: Web App

398fc27a-5680-40ee-a73f-6d2fba9f980f.action: detect in it the instances of every block definition
398fc27a-5680-40ee-a73f-6d2fba9f980f.label: Detect in new runs

3a807173-78c6-4e65-a07c-6d1aed8a072b.action: derive route segments from the runs' GPS tracks, each with a reference track sampled every 10 m, its length and the number of runs that pass it
3a807173-78c6-4e65-a07c-6d1aed8a072b.label: Derive route segments
3a807173-78c6-4e65-a07c-6d1aed8a072b.rationale: Route segments are the basis of route-segment block definitions and recommendations.

3ada0e31-9a55-47b5-bb5c-e160ba2e68ed.gherkin: And switching off 'Join points' or 'Trend line' hides those lines on every chart
3ada0e31-9a55-47b5-bb5c-e160ba2e68ed.given: a block in Analysis whose pace got faster and whose heart rate stayed the same
3ada0e31-9a55-47b5-bb5c-e160ba2e68ed.label: Several metrics analysed together
3ada0e31-9a55-47b5-bb5c-e160ba2e68ed.then: Analysis shows one 'Over time' chart for pace and one for heart rate on the same dates, each with the block's points joined by a line and its trend line, and the table of changes reads a change for pace and no detectable change for heart rate
3ada0e31-9a55-47b5-bb5c-e160ba2e68ed.when: the runner chooses pace and heart rate

3b2a5032-9b62-4e79-a7f6-b568f1399963.given: a data folder with three runs, each with 10 minutes at 4:00/km in its middle; one item holds the efforts of the first two, another the easy first 10 minutes of the third
3b2a5032-9b62-4e79-a7f6-b568f1399963.label: Curves from the data folder
3b2a5032-9b62-4e79-a7f6-b568f1399963.then: each run named is read once, with progress, and a run that is no longer there is passed over; the first item's curve reaches 10 minutes at 4:00 /km from one of its two runs, the second's stays at 6:00 /km from the third run; an item with no stretches has an empty curve
3b2a5032-9b62-4e79-a7f6-b568f1399963.when: the pace curves of both items are computed together

3cd8560b-fa73-4d5d-8ff2-70be65c42c06.gherkin:
And a block without the attribute has heart rate over the whole block, wherever it starts in the run
And the block's card shows "heart rate from minute 5"
3cd8560b-fa73-4d5d-8ff2-70be65c42c06.given: the "30-minute effort" block with its heart rate start at minute 5, and efforts starting at minute 3 and at minute 13 of their runs
3cd8560b-fa73-4d5d-8ff2-70be65c42c06.label: Heart rate from the same minute of every effort
3cd8560b-fa73-4d5d-8ff2-70be65c42c06.then: both have heart rate, each the mean from minute 5 of the effort to its end (25 minutes), whatever minute of the run the effort started

3d858429-f454-438e-a431-eed8e4172c06.gherkin: And its size is within about 100–300 KB
3d858429-f454-438e-a431-eed8e4172c06.label: Run file is columnar
3d858429-f454-438e-a431-eed8e4172c06.then: it is columnar JSON: one array per field, of equal length
3d858429-f454-438e-a431-eed8e4172c06.when: its derived file runs/<id>.json is read

3e50c847-c0a6-4c80-8354-9e28dafeb247.gherkin: And the Runs screen shows the import progress
3e50c847-c0a6-4c80-8354-9e28dafeb247.given: fit/ holds 50 FIT files not yet imported
3e50c847-c0a6-4c80-8354-9e28dafeb247.label: UI responsive during import
3e50c847-c0a6-4c80-8354-9e28dafeb247.then: the Gear and tags screen opens while the import continues in the background
3e50c847-c0a6-4c80-8354-9e28dafeb247.when: the user starts the import and, while it runs, switches to the Gear and tags screen

3e608f71-04ae-42e1-aabe-194a07a8a79f.description: After the user changes a metric, context filter or splitting field, the trend or the A/B comparison (with its bootstrap uncertainty interval) is recomputed from block-instances.json within 3 s. Threshold from the user's answer: ≤3 s.
3e608f71-04ae-42e1-aabe-194a07a8a79f.label: Analysis recompute time

4050830f-77be-4448-b5e1-7f84e38459d5.condition: for each FIT file in fit/ not yet listed in manifest.json
4050830f-77be-4448-b5e1-7f84e38459d5.label: Import each new file

41a57acc-3f2c-43ce-be90-4b19dc889fa6.action: divide each run's samples into 10 s windows holding the mean of each metric
41a57acc-3f2c-43ce-be90-4b19dc889fa6.label: 10 s windows
41a57acc-3f2c-43ce-be90-4b19dc889fa6.rationale: Resolution levels: sample → step → window → block → run.

422370cf-5624-4397-804e-862b68fe2f68.action: keep the dependency graph between parts free of cycles, with 0 cycles that run through more than one part (a cycle inside one part is that part's own business)
422370cf-5624-4397-804e-862b68fe2f68.label: No cycles between parts
422370cf-5624-4397-804e-862b68fe2f68.rationale: Parts in a cycle can only be understood, tested and released together, which makes them one part (Martin, Clean Architecture: the Acyclic Dependencies Principle; ISO/IEC 25010 modularity).

4265e3ce-648a-4471-8c97-0100fede2b68.description: A candidate fragment being checked against its definition's tolerances.
4265e3ce-648a-4471-8c97-0100fede2b68.do: check every matching condition of the definition: pace band, grade, route segment and direction, pace steadiness, effort before the block, block start for heart rate
4265e3ce-648a-4471-8c97-0100fede2b68.label: Matching

4657ac26-ce37-4d24-a2cf-0e02511d9e0a.alternatives:
1. A component library (shadcn, Radix themes, MUI): a modern look quickly, but a dependency on the budget and a second styling system beside the tokens.
2. Fonts from Google Fonts at run time: zero bytes shipped, but every visit tells a third party about the runner (Data stays local).
3. System fonts only: no files, but a different look on every platform and weaker tabular numbers.
4657ac26-ce37-4d24-a2cf-0e02511d9e0a.consequences:
• The look is one stylesheet of tokens and classes; a theme change is a token change.
• public/fonts carries the OFL licence text; the fonts add 84 KB of static assets, outside the script budget.
• Charts keep their aria names and classes, so the E2E tests and the dataviz rules (one axis per chart, series colours in fixed order, text in text tokens) are unchanged.
4657ac26-ce37-4d24-a2cf-0e02511d9e0a.context: The runner found the screens dated: "nie wyglada na nowoczesny ... chodzi mi o wyglad, kolory, sposobu prezentacji wykresu", then "jest lepiej ale ciagle nie top class". Every colour must stay a theme token (fitness function on untokenized colours), the app sends nothing over the network, and each route has a 200 KB script budget.
4657ac26-ce37-4d24-a2cf-0e02511d9e0a.decision: One visual system in app/globals.css: a neutral surface scale (bg, surface, surface-2, surface-3) with hairline lines instead of boxes in boxes, ink buttons for the primary action, one accent for selection and links, the four series colours reserved for data. Type: Geist Sans and Geist Mono, SIL OFL, bundled under public/fonts (latin and latin-ext, 84 KB) and declared with @font-face, so no font is fetched from the network; numbers tabular, mono on axes and readouts. The shell: a sidebar with stroked icons, the data folder and the search, no top bar. Figures in one strip card; tables with numbers right-aligned and uppercase small headers. Charts: a gradient wash under each line, smooth monotone-cubic paths on the run lanes with the ticks inside the plot, one cursor card for all lanes, recessive grid and axis tokens, a halo under the route on a dotted grid. Analysis changes as figures with a verdict chip.
4657ac26-ce37-4d24-a2cf-0e02511d9e0a.description: The visual system of the screens: tokens, bundled fonts, shell, figures, charts.
4657ac26-ce37-4d24-a2cf-0e02511d9e0a.label: Look and feel

5ba5e99c-da08-4beb-bd36-da1fd533abce.alternatives:
1. Every block computed on demand, nothing stored: one path, but A/B, the run screen and each reload of Analysis would read every run file again.
2. Keep the Blocks screen and add the builder to it: the old flow of defining first and analysing later, which the runner found of little sense.
3. Rewrite the found definitions (route, lap pattern, effort) as rules too: one type in the code, but a route needs a reference track and a pattern a lap layout, which a rule of ranges cannot say.
4. A language model or a grammar for free text (built, dropped at the runner's request).
5ba5e99c-da08-4beb-bd36-da1fd533abce.consequences:
• The runner chooses data and analyses it in one place; a link reproduces an analysis, rules included.
• Two ways to a block's segments: stored for kept blocks, computed for rules in the link; both run the same detection, so the results agree.
• A new shape or condition is a field of the rule, a branch of the detection and a unit test.
• The same rule always selects the same segments, so scenarios state them word for word; nothing changes for Data stays local.
5ba5e99c-da08-4beb-bd36-da1fd533abce.context: The runner remodelled the app: "blocks nie maja duzego sensu ... blocki sa wyliczane na biezaco z danych w analityce ... wybieram dane - czyli tworze np bloki - najszybsze 5 min przy tetnie powyzej 160 ... system wybiera mi wszystkie segmenty i je uzywa". Three overlapping notions had grown: blocks detected beforehand, blocks from criteria and run sets. The app sends nothing over the network, reading every run file on the main thread would freeze the screen, results must be deterministic, and the A/B comparison and the run screen need a block's segments without opening every run file.
5ba5e99c-da08-4beb-bd36-da1fd533abce.decision: One notion: a block is a rule (which runs, the shape of a segment, its conditions on average and at every moment, how many per run, the statistic) built on the Analysis screen, or one of the definitions found in the runs or made on a run's chart (route segment, workout lap, lap pattern, effort, steady fragment). There is no Blocks screen: the picker of the Analysis screen lists the kept blocks, the suggestions and single runs, and holds the builder. A rule used without keeping it lives in the link (a compact code) and its segments are computed on demand in the Processing Worker by an 'instances' job, one pass over the run files for all such rules, skipping the runs no rule draws from, abandoned when the items change. A kept block's segments stay in derived/block-instances.json, rebuilt after every import and change of gear, tags or definitions, as before. The pace curve is computed by a 'curve' job from the stretches an item holds. A rule's conditions select: its segments are all accepted, and the general tolerances are off for it.
5ba5e99c-da08-4beb-bd36-da1fd533abce.label: Blocks defined in Analysis

62453160-130b-4517-ae25-023829dea55e.alternatives:
1. Angular: everything included and one way of doing it, heavier.
2. Vue with Nuxt: similar capabilities, gentler learning curve, smaller ecosystem.
3. Svelte with SvelteKit: smaller bundles, smaller ecosystem.
62453160-130b-4517-ae25-023829dea55e.consequences:
• The largest ecosystem of components and libraries, and the largest hiring pool.
• React itself is only the view: routing, data, forms and state are choices to make and keep current.
• Server components cut the JavaScript sent, but add a server and a new mental model.
• Next.js majors arrive roughly yearly and change conventions; upgrades are planned work.
62453160-130b-4517-ae25-023829dea55e.context: This element is a web front end that people use in their own browsers, on their own devices and networks. The forces: every kilobyte of JavaScript is downloaded, parsed and run on the user's phone, and mid-range phones on mobile networks are where most budgets break; search engines and first visits reward content in the first HTML response, while app-like screens favour rendering in the browser; a framework brings its ecosystem, hiring pool and release cadence, and its majors reach end of support on published dates; a shared design system keeps screens consistent and accessible, but costs effort to build and keep; the browsers to support decide which features and polyfills ship; and accessibility is a legal duty in many markets (European Accessibility Act, ADA, Section 508), cheap when built in and expensive when retrofitted.
62453160-130b-4517-ae25-023829dea55e.decision: The front end is built with React in TypeScript (strict). Rendering: at build time: Next.js static export (output: 'export'), no server components or server-side code, runs from any static host or the local disk. Design system: the application's own components, styled only through its theme's design tokens (CSS custom properties for the light and dark theme); no component library (revised 19 Nov 2026: six screens, and the 200 KB budget per route). Browsers: the last 2 versions of Chrome, Edge and Opera only (File System Access API); other browsers get a not-supported message. Budget: LCP 2500 ms, INP 200 ms, CLS 0.1 at the 75th percentile of page loads, 200 KB of JavaScript per route; WCAG 2.2 AA. Dependency updates: as decided in the Dependency hygiene pack. Versions tracked through endoflife.date (react, nextjs), each major replaced at least 180 days before its end of support.
62453160-130b-4517-ae25-023829dea55e.label: Built with React

6571fdbf-e3a5-4871-8aec-2f04b8ff4a85.alternatives:
1. Levels: one rule for many parts, but less precise between peers.
2. Only forbidding known-bad dependencies: easy to start, but anything not foreseen is allowed.
3. No checked rules: fastest to start, and boundaries erode within months.
6571fdbf-e3a5-4871-8aec-2f04b8ff4a85.consequences:
• Every dependency between parts is a visible decision, reviewed when it is added.
• The declarations are code to maintain: adding a dependency means changing one line in module.json and convincing a reviewer.
• Boundaries hold only while the check runs in every build.
• With many parts the lists become noise; levels scale better.
6571fdbf-e3a5-4871-8aec-2f04b8ff4a85.context: The code in this element is cut into parts (modules, packages, libraries) and keeps changing. Without written and checked rules, every shortcut adds a dependency nobody decided on: one module reads another's internals, two packages import each other, and a "common" folder grows until every change touches everything. The forces: rules kept only in a wiki erode within months; a cycle makes two parts one, so neither can be tested, owned or released alone; sharing code saves typing but couples the teams that share it; a boundary nobody owns is crossed by whoever is in a hurry; and an old codebase cannot fix every violation at once. What the parts are (layers, rings, slices) is the Architecture style pack; who owns each part is the Code review and branching pack; this pack keeps the boundaries between the parts.
6571fdbf-e3a5-4871-8aec-2f04b8ff4a85.decision: Each part (a folder of lib/, and app, components and workers) declares in its module.json the parts it may depend on ("uses") and whether it runs on the main thread, in the Processing Worker or both, and exposes a published API in its index.ts; any other dependency, any import of another part's file but its index, any cycle through more than one part, and any main-thread import at run time of a part that runs in the worker fails the dependency check, which runs in every check of a change (every violation fails the build). Shared code: a small shared kernel. The checker is scripts/boundaries.mjs, which reads the module.json files; it runs in the unit tests, so a violation shows up like any failing test.
6571fdbf-e3a5-4871-8aec-2f04b8ff4a85.label: Declared dependencies only

66ea8d17-0186-448e-b9d1-0a9a26f5e3af.alternatives:
1. Versioned internal libraries: each part upgrades on its own schedule.

66ea8d17-0186-448e-b9d1-0a9a26f5e3af.consequences:

• Every kernel change is a change to every part that uses it, hence the approvals and the size limit.

66ea8d17-0186-448e-b9d1-0a9a26f5e3af.context: The code in this element is cut into parts (modules, packages, libraries) and keeps changing. Without written and checked rules, every shortcut adds a dependency nobody decided on: one module reads another's internals, two packages import each other, and a "common" folder grows until every change touches everything. The forces: rules kept only in a wiki erode within months; a cycle makes two parts one, so neither can be tested, owned or released alone; sharing code saves typing but couples the teams that share it; a boundary nobody owns is crossed by whoever is in a hurry; and an old codebase cannot fix every violation at once. What the parts are (layers, rings, slices) is the Architecture style pack; who owns each part is the Code review and branching pack; this pack keeps the boundaries between the parts.
66ea8d17-0186-448e-b9d1-0a9a26f5e3af.decision: Code shared between parts lives in one shared kernel, lib/kernel: the run contracts (samples, laps, windows, run and index files) and the format versions used by at least two parts, types and constants only, with no dependency on a part and no package (an empty allowlist), at most 5% of the source lines. A change to the kernel is a change to every part that uses it and is reviewed as such.

7e820091-6148-431b-b28d-880efea10233.label: Estimated pace curve
7e820091-6148-431b-b28d-880efea10233.rationale: The runner asked: "jesli chodzi o pace curve ... dodaj estymaowana ... bazujac na researchu", and, seeing bests above a regression line ("mam wyniki ponad ta linia"), chose the envelope: "tak zrob (1, obwiednia)"; then "daj mozliwosc przemieszczania sie po tej estymacie ... albo pokaz roznice pomiedzy pomiarem a estymata", both done. The models are the literature's (ADR "Pace curve models"): Riegel's power law (Riegel 1981), meant for a maximal effort, and the critical speed model (Monod & Scherrer 1965; Hill 1993; Jones & Vanhatalo 2017). The model's choices after that literature: the power law's exponent from bests of 3 minutes and more, the critical speed from bests of 2 to 20 minutes, 3 bests at least for either, and the distances predicted, 5 km, 10 km, the half and the marathon.

839d8289-93cd-4d39-9e0b-4c96b2d659f9.alternatives:
1. A charting library (uPlot, Recharts) and a map library with tiles (Leaflet, MapLibre): richer out of the box, but tiles are network requests, and the libraries weigh on the 200 KB budget per route.
2. Canvas drawing: faster for very long series, harder to make accessible and to style through CSS tokens.
839d8289-93cd-4d39-9e0b-4c96b2d659f9.consequences:
• With the map background off, no network request for a map: the data stays on the computer (Data stays local).
• With it on, the tile server learns the area of the route shown, nothing else; its usage policy applies (light personal use, attribution shown).
• The charts and the map stay small and themeable; features such as zoom are built only when needed.
839d8289-93cd-4d39-9e0b-4c96b2d659f9.context: Screens need range selection on a chart and stretch selection on a map, synchronized, in light and dark themes.
839d8289-93cd-4d39-9e0b-4c96b2d659f9.decision: Own SVG components, no charting or map library: the run chart with its metrics laid over one chart, range selection, zoom, block and lap bands (components/RunChart.tsx, ADR "Run metrics on one chart"), the route map drawn from the run's own coordinates in Web Mercator (components/charts.tsx), and the trend, analysis and profile charts (components/TrendChart.tsx, components/AnalysisCharts.tsx), all styled through the theme's tokens for the light and dark theme. The map background, when the runner switches it on (off by default), is OpenStreetMap's standard tiles drawn as images under the route, with their attribution; darkened through a CSS filter in the dark theme.
839d8289-93cd-4d39-9e0b-4c96b2d659f9.label: Charts and map library

84bc4ef9-d9e6-4de4-a4e1-2b2e46e1ad73.alternatives:
1. Two or more y axes, one per metric: the reader cannot tell which line goes with which axis, and the crossing of lines suggests a relation that is an artefact of the scales.
2. Indexed to a common base (percent of the run's mean): one scale, but the values read off it are not the metric's own.
3. Keep the stack of lanes: the runner asked for one chart.
84bc4ef9-d9e6-4de4-a4e1-2b2e46e1ad73.consequences:
• In bands the lines do not tangle and each has its scale beside it; overlaid, where two lines cross means nothing, as the note under the chart says.
• Walking breaks and stops run to the edge of a band instead of flattening the running.
• Smooth draws the rolling mean of the windows over 1/30 of the range shown (components/chartZoom.ts, rollingMean), so the noise of 10 s windows goes at the scale of a whole run and comes back when zoomed in; the tooltip reads the line drawn, the statistics read the windows.
• The average, min and max of one metric at a time are marked from the statistics (lib/blocks, rangeStats), so the marks and the table agree; the trend and Pa:HR decoupling are numbers of a selection, not lines.
• More than 4 lines are not drawn at once; the runner turns one off to show another.
• The block-making selection, the map and the cursor work as before.
84bc4ef9-d9e6-4de4-a4e1-2b2e46e1ad73.context: The runner asked for the metrics of a run laid over one chart ("chce aby metryki byly nakladane na 1 wykres"), with statistics of a selection and zoom. The metrics have different units (min/km, bpm, spm, ms), so one chart has no common y scale.
84bc4ef9-d9e6-4de4-a4e1-2b2e46e1ad73.decision: One SVG chart (components/RunChart.tsx) replaces the stack of lanes: each shown metric (up to 4, the categorical series colours 1–4, a colour kept by a metric while it is shown) is scaled to its own range within the time range shown, between its 5th and 95th percentile, padded. By default each line has its own band of the chart, the bands overlapping by a quarter, its short name and two round values (or its zone boundaries) in a gutter left of the plot (labels too near each other left out); "Overlaid" lays every line over the whole height with the focused metric's values only. Zones from the settings are stripes of a band in the metric's colour. The focused metric draws the grid and the wash. The x axis spaces the chart by time or by distance: the domain stays in time and a time is placed at the distance run by then (components/chartZoom.ts, distanceMap), two axes under the plot. Zoom is a time domain held by the Run screen, changed by a selection, buttons, pinch or Ctrl/⌘ + scroll, a sideways scroll and an overview strip; the lines rescale to the range shown and the route map fits the stretch run in it. Kept blocks are drawn only on demand. The marks take no pointer events, so a press and its release always land on the svg. The statistics of a range come from lib/blocks (rangeStats), over the 10 s windows with movement.
84bc4ef9-d9e6-4de4-a4e1-2b2e46e1ad73.label: Run metrics on one chart

8cd8c786-c600-4808-95b3-d73aac37d4b1.rationale: The runner asked: "moge zrobic zoom in wykresu i zoom aut", then: "zaznaczenie automatycznie zoomuje, teraz musze to kliknac", "zmiana okna na dole w podgladzie lub zaznaczenie tam zmienia selekcje", "wcisnienie whole run usuwa selekcje lapa", "usun tez + - i ... scroll myszki powinno robic zoom w aktualnym punkcie wybranym na diagramie" and "zoom powinien automatycznie zwiekszac i zmniejszac okno na dole podgladu". Then: "zoom myszka nie dziala" (a notch on macOS reports a few pixels). The model's choices: the mouse wheel (or a pinch) over the whole chart, the strip of laps, the plot and the overview, zooms around the point under the pointer by a factor growing with the square root of the wheel's delta, so that a notch of 4 px zooms by about 15 % and one of 100 px by 2, down to 1 minute; a sideways scroll moves; the keys + and − on the focused chart zoom for the keyboard; then: "zoom to selection i whole run ... juz chyba nie ma sensu" and "usun przycisk whole run ... zamknieci selelckji na dole wraca do calego treningu": there are no zoom buttons; closing the selection with its ✕ shows the whole run, and with no selection the wheel or the key 0 does; a selection (dragged, on the map, a lap, a block, from the link) zooms to it at once with 15 % of its length as room either side; the overview strip's window is the range shown and grows and shrinks with the zoom, the selection marked on it on its own: dragging the window moves the range shown and the selection with it, dragging elsewhere selects that stretch, a click centres the window.

8d04762f-4c1c-468b-8e99-b6fb65dfa133.description:
Strideprism MVP – specification
18 Nov 2026 · @Tomasz
1. Goal and scope
The MVP must prove one thing: comparing blocks within the same context detects changes in running that watch averages do not show.
The MVP user is a single runner working on their own COROS FIT files, locally on their own computer.
The MVP supports three scenarios:
1.  Trend on a fixed route. How heart rate and form change on the same stretch of the long run, at a similar pace.
2.  Trend of a repeated workout. How the 25-minute tempo run changes: pace, heart rate, form and drift within the effort.
3.  Effect of a change. What new shoes changed, under the same conditions before and after.
2. Concepts
The block is the smallest unit of comparison. A block is a fragment of a run together with its context, not just a stretch of route.
Concept
Meaning
Block definition
A recipe that says which fragments of a run qualify, e.g. “25-minute tempo” or “promenade northbound, pace 4:45–5:15, at least 8 minutes into the run”
Block instance
A specific fragment of a specific run that meets the definition, with its context stored
Context
Everything that decides whether two instances may be compared. It has four layers (below)
Metric provenance
Which device and which algorithm produced a number. Wrist heart rate and arm-band heart rate are two different series
Noise threshold
The normal spread of a metric between instances under the same conditions. A difference below the threshold is not a result
The four context layers of an instance:
• The block itself: pace, grade, duration, direction on the route, the profile of metrics inside the block.
• What came before: minute and kilometre of the run, effort in the 2 minutes before the block, position in the workout structure.
• The run: shoes, heart rate sensor, workout type, technique cue.
• The day: load from previous days, temperature.
A trend is a series of instances of one definition over time. An A/B comparison is two sets of instances of one definition that differ in one context field.
3. Data model
Raw data is immutable, and everything derived can be rebuilt from it from scratch. Block definitions and rules will change, so no result may be the only copy.
Entity
Kind
Key fields
Run
raw
start time (key), source file, device, distance, duration
Sample
raw
run, timestamp (1 s), speed, heart rate, cadence, ground contact time, vertical oscillation, step length, power, altitude, GPS position, temperature, effort pace, leg spring stiffness
Lap
raw
run, start, end, duration, distance
Gear
user-entered
name, type (shoes, heart rate sensor), date range of use
RunTag
user-entered
run, workout type, technique cue, shoes (override), note
Window
derived
run, 10 s window, metric means, quality flags
RouteSegment
derived
reference track every 10 m, length, number of runs
BlockDefinition
user-entered or recommended
name, type, parameters, tolerances, origin (manual, recommendation)
BlockInstance
derived
definition, run, start, end, four context layers, metric means, per-minute profile, status (accepted, rejected with reason)
DayState
derived
date, load from the previous 3 and 7 days, days since the last hard session
Principles:
• Resolution levels: sample → step → window → block → run. The step level is empty in the MVP and waits for the sensors of step 2.
• Provenance: every metric in Sample records its source device. A device change starts a new series.
• Versioning: every derived table records the version of the algorithm that produced it.
• Place is optional: a run without GPS still produces blocks based on workout structure.
4. Functional requirements
The MVP has 15 requirements in four groups.
Import
• F1. Import FIT files from the chosen folder. Re-importing the same run does not create a duplicate (key: start time).
• F2. Read all fields from section 3, including COROS developer fields (effort pace, leg spring stiffness) and laps.
• F3. Quality flags on 10 s windows: stopped, first 150 s of the run, grade, missing sensor signal.
Context
• F4. Gear register with date ranges. Shoes and sensor are assigned to runs automatically by date, with an override for a single run.
• F5. Run tags: workout type, technique cue, note.
• F6. Day state computed from the user's own data: load from the previous 3 and 7 days and days since the last hard session.
Blocks
• F7. Three types of block definition: route segment (GPS), workout structure element (a lap of a given duration or distance), steady fragment within a given pace range.
• F8. Manual creation of a definition from a fragment selected on the run's chart or map.
• F9. Recommendations: the system proposes a definition when it finds at least 5 instances of a route segment or at least 3 workouts with the same structure.
• F10. Automatic detection of instances in historical runs and in every newly imported run.
Comparisons
• F11. Trend: a series of instances of one definition over time, for a chosen metric, filtered by context fields.
• F12. A/B comparison: two sets of instances that differ in one context field. The result is the difference, an uncertainty interval and a verdict against the noise threshold.
• F13. Profile inside the block: overlaid per-minute profiles of selected instances.
• F14. Transparency: every result shows the list of instances that went into it, plus the rejected ones with the reason for rejection.
• F15. Export of instances and results to CSV.
5. Comparison rules
A comparison works in two steps: first strict matching of conditions, then a model correction only for the residual pace difference. The result is always shown in both versions: raw and corrected.
The default matching tolerances come from the preliminary analysis of 18 Nov 2026, and the user can change them in the block definition.
Condition
Default value
Pace
the same band, 30 s/km wide
Grade
effort pace differs from pace by at most 4%
Route segment
at least 90% of points within 30 m of the reference track, same direction
Pace steadiness within the block
coefficient of variation of speed below 0.15
Effort before the block
mean speed over the 2 minutes before the block within 12% of the block's speed
Block start (for heart rate)
at least 8 minutes after the start of the run
Other rules:
• Minimum length depends on the metric. Ground contact time, cadence, vertical oscillation and step length: at least 60 s. Heart rate: at least 4 minutes. A shorter block yields a result only for the metrics that meet their threshold.
• Minimum number of instances. Trend: at least 5. A/B comparison: at least 4 on each side. Below these numbers the system shows the points without a verdict.
• Noise threshold. Computed for each metric and definition as the standard deviation between instances in the same context. In the preliminary analysis, ground contact time at a fixed pace varied between runs by about 2–3 ms; the value is to be confirmed on the full data.
• A/B verdict. “Change” when the uncertainty interval of the difference excludes zero and the difference exceeds the noise threshold. Otherwise “no detectable change”.
• Device change. Instances from different sensors form separate series and are not joined by a trend line.
• Warning about confounding with the fitness trend. When groups A and B do not interleave in time (e.g. shoes changed once and for good), the result carries a warning and a suggestion to rotate.
• Nesting. Blocks may overlap, but one fragment of a run enters a given comparison only once.
6. Interface
The MVP is a browser application with six screens. On first launch the user picks the data folder; later launches open the same folder.
Screen
What it shows
What you can do
Runs
List of runs, import status, assigned shoes and tags
Import the folder, correct a run's context
Run
Metrics over time, map, detected block instances
Select a fragment and create a block definition from it
Blocks
Definitions with instance counts, system recommendations
Accept or reject a recommendation, change tolerances
Trend
Instances of one definition over time, noise threshold, gear changes as vertical lines
Choose the metric and context filter, open the list of instances
A/B comparison
Difference with uncertainty interval, verdict, warnings, overlaid per-minute profiles
Choose the context field that splits the groups
Gear and tags
Register of shoes and sensors with dates, tag dictionary
Add gear, change a date range
Hovering over any point on a chart shows the full context of the instance: run, date, pace, direction, minute of the run, shoes and sensor.
7. Architecture and technology
The MVP is a React/TypeScript/Next.js application that runs entirely in the browser. The user points it at a folder on disk; the application reads FIT files from it and writes all its data there. There is no server and no database, and the data never leaves the computer.
Limitation: folder access (File System Access API, showDirectoryPicker) works in Chrome, Edge and Opera. Firefox and Safari do not support it (caniuse, as of 18 Nov 2026).
Layer
Choice
Rationale
Application
Next.js with static export, React, TypeScript
No server; the same model as Radical Studio; can be published as a plain web page
Data access
File System Access API, folder handle remembered in IndexedDB
The folder is picked once; on reopening it is enough to confirm access
FIT parser
Official Garmin FIT JavaScript SDK
The official SDK of the FIT format; reading COROS files with developer fields is to be confirmed at the start of stage 1
Processing
TypeScript in a Web Worker
Import and recomputation do not block the interface
Statistics
Own TypeScript module: linear regression, bootstrap for uncertainty intervals
The methods needed are simple and require no external libraries
Charts and map
To be chosen in stage 5
Requirement: selecting a range on a chart and a stretch on the map
Storage
Files in the user's folder (layout below)
The data is portable, readable and can be versioned or synced with any tool
Data flow:
1.  Import: new FIT files in the folder → Run, Sample, Lap.
2.  Preparation: Sample → Window with quality flags; GPS tracks → RouteSegment.
3.  Context: Gear, RunTag and DayState joined to runs by date.
4.  Detection: BlockDefinition + run data → BlockInstance with four context layers.
5.  Write: the results of steps 1–4 go to the folder as denormalized files.
6.  Analysis and presentation: trend, A/B comparison and noise threshold computed in the browser from the instance files; the screens of section 6 and CSV export.
The “Recompute everything” action rebuilds steps 1–5 from scratch from the FIT files.
Data folder layout:
my-folder/
  fit/                     # the user's FIT files, never modified by the app
  strideprism/
    manifest.json          # schema and algorithm versions, list of imported files
    user/                  # user-entered data, never recomputed
      gear.json
      run-tags.json
      block-definitions.json
    derived/               # derived data, fully rebuildable
      runs/<id>.json       # one run: samples and 10 s windows, columnar
      runs-index.json      # one row per run, with context
      segments.json
      block-instances.json # one row per instance, with full context
      day-state.json
Storage rules:
• Denormalization. runs-index.json and block-instances.json hold every field needed for trends and A/B comparisons (shoes, sensor, tags, day state), so the analysis screens do not open individual run files.
• Two directories, two rules. user/ is the only source of manually entered data and the application never overwrites it on recomputation. derived/ can be deleted entirely.
• Version mismatch. When the algorithm version in manifest.json is older than the application's, the application offers to recompute.
• Format. Columnar JSON (one array per field), about 100–300 KB per run. Moving to Parquet is an open decision (section 11).
All code is in TypeScript. Tests run on a few sample FIT files with hand-checked expected values.
Repository structure:
strideprism/
  app/              # Next.js pages (the screens of section 6)
  components/       # charts, map, tables
  lib/
    fs/             # folder access, reading and writing files, manifest
    ingest/         # FIT parser, import, deduplication
    prepare/        # 10 s windows, quality flags, route segments
    context/        # gear, tags, day state
    blocks/         # definitions, instance detection, recommendations
    compare/        # matching, pace correction, noise, A/B, trend
    stats/          # regression, bootstrap
  workers/          # Web Worker for import and recomputation
  tests/            # tests and sample FIT files with expected values
8. Out of scope for the MVP
The MVP deliberately leaves out everything that is not needed to test the method on one runner.
• Own IMU sensors and video analysis (step 2 of Strideprism).
• Per-step data and left/right leg split.
• Accounts, multiple users, cloud hosting, a mobile app.
• Automatic sync with COROS, Garmin or Strava; the MVP imports from a folder.
• Weather from an external source, sleep and HRV. The watch temperature serves only as an approximation.
• Training plans and advice. The tool shows what changed, not what to do.
• Sports other than running.
9. Acceptance criteria
The MVP is done when it meets all seven conditions on the author's data (runs since 3 Aug 2026).
1.  Import. All historical runs import without errors, and a repeated import adds no records.
2.  Recommendations. The system proposes the seaside promenade segment (about 1.1 km) and the 25-minute tempo on its own, without hints from the user.
3.  Agreement with the preliminary analysis. The heart rate trend on the promenade segment in the 4:45–5:15/km band reproduces the result of 18 Nov 2026: 34 steady passes, heart rate 149–154 in August and September and about 135 on 14 Nov.
4.  Shoe scenario. The A/B comparison for two pairs of shoes returns a difference, an uncertainty interval and a verdict, and shows a warning when the groups do not interleave.
5.  Negative test. An A/B comparison on a random split of runs returns “no detectable change” in at least 9 of 10 trials.
6.  Transparency. For every result the list of accepted and rejected instances can be opened, with the reason for rejection.
7.  Reproducibility. The “Recompute everything” action rebuilds the derived data directory from scratch from the FIT files and gives the same results, while user-entered data stays untouched.
Success criterion for the whole of step 1, beyond the software itself: within 4–6 weeks of use the tool detects at least one change in the author's running that is larger than the noise.
10. Delivery stages
Five stages, about 8–11 weeks of spare-time work in total. The estimates are rough.
Stage
Scope
Requirements
Time
1. Data foundation
App skeleton, folder access, FIT import in a Web Worker, file writing, 10 s windows, quality flags, gear and tag register
F1–F6
2–3 wks
2. Blocks
Three definition types, instance detection, instance context, recommendations
F7, F9, F10
2 wks
3. Trend
Strict matching, pace correction, noise threshold, profile inside the block
F11, F13, F14
1–2 wks
4. A/B comparison
Verdict, uncertainty intervals, warnings, negative test
F12
2 wks
5. Interface and release
Six screens, manual block creation, export, repository with instructions
F8, F15
1–2 wks
The results of stages 1–4 are checked by tests on sample FIT files before the full screens exist. Collecting data for the shoe scenario (rotating two pairs) is worth starting in stage 1, because it takes several weeks of runs.
11. Open decisions
Six things need the author's decision before the relevant stage starts.
[ ] List of shoes with dates of first use (needed for scenario 3; before stage 1).
[ ] Exact date of the switch from wrist heart rate to the arm band (the preliminary analysis assumed about 15 Oct 2026; before stage 1).
[ ] Source of files: manual export from COROS into the folder, or a download script (before stage 1).
[ ] Format of derived files: columnar JSON or Parquet (before stage 1; JSON is enough for a few hundred runs).
[ ] Open-source licence: permissive (MIT, Apache 2.0) or copyleft (AGPL) (before release).
[ ] Language of the interface and documentation: Polish, English or both (before stage 5).

Q: Specyfikacja mówi, że dostęp do folderu działa tylko w Chrome, Edge i Operze. Jakie wsparcie przeglądarek zapisać i co ma się stać w Firefoxie lub Safari?
A: Chromium + komunikat: wspierane tylko Chrome, Edge i Opera; w innych przeglądarkach aplikacja pokazuje komunikat o braku wsparcia i nie startuje.
Q: Otwarta decyzja z sekcji 11: skąd pochodzą pliki FIT? Od tego zależy, czy wymagania obejmą skrypt pobierania.
A: Ręczny eksport: użytkownik sam eksportuje pliki z COROS do folderu fit/.
Q: Format plików pochodnych (otwarta decyzja z sekcji 11): co zapisać w modelu?
A: Kolumnowy JSON.
Q: Ile może trwać import i przeliczenie? Specyfikacja nie podaje limitu czasu, a od tego zależą progi fitness functions dla wydajności.
A: ≤5 s/bieg, ≤15 min całość
Q: Ile czasu mogą zajmować ekrany analizy, czyli przeliczenie trendu lub porównania A/B z bootstrapem po zmianie filtra?
A: ≤3 s
Q: Co się dzieje z odrzuconą rekomendacją definicji bloku przy następnym wykrywaniu, np. po imporcie nowych biegów?
A: Zapamiętana (Recommended)
Q: Czy użytkownik może usunąć zaakceptowaną lub ręcznie utworzoną definicję bloku?
A: Nie w MVP (Recommended) (no requirement)
Q: tak etap 7 - dodaktowo jesli chdozi o mockupy .. chce nowoczesne UI. Jaki kierunek wizualny ma mieć nowoczesny interfejs Strideprism?
A: jasny lub ciemny, do wyboru i automatycznego wyboru bazujac na motywie kompuetara,
Q: Jak ma wyglądać nawigacja między sześcioma ekranami (Runs, Run, Blocks, Trend, A/B, Gear and tags)?
A: Boczny pasek + Cmd+K (Recommended) (no requirement)
Q: Jak pokazywać szczegóły instancji i listę przyjętych i odrzuconych instancji (przejrzystość wyniku)?
A: Wysuwany panel boczny (Recommended) (no requirement)
Q: Day State liczy „dni od ostatniego mocnego treningu”, ale specyfikacja nie definiuje mocnego treningu („hard session”). Jak go rozpoznać?
A: a po co ci dni od ostatniego mocnego treningu ? to bezsensu
Q: „Dni od ostatniego mocnego treningu” pochodzą z Twojej specyfikacji (F6 i encja DayState). Co z nim zrobić?
A: Usuń z modelu (Recommended)
