Dragging the window moves the range shown and the selection with it; dragging elsewhere on the strip selects that stretch (and zooms to it); a click centres the window there.
Q: (użytkownik) zoom myszka nie dziala
A: (model) A notch of a mouse wheel on macOS reports a few pixels (about 4), not 100 as on Windows, so the zoom of 2^(delta/100) moved the range by 3 % a notch and seemed dead. The zoom per wheel event now grows with the square root of the delta (lines and pages turned into pixels): a notch of 4 px zooms by about 15 %, one of 100 px by 2, a trackpad's small steps smoothly; and the wheel zooms over the whole chart: the strip of laps, the plot and the overview (there around the point of the whole run under the pointer).
Q: (użytkownik) graf sie zmienia ale selekcja nie ... gdy scrolluje myszka
Q: (użytkownik) zoom uniewaznia selekcje .... w tym momencie sa to 2 rzeczy
Q: (użytkownik) ok dobra zosn jak jest ... seleleckaj musi byc recznie wybrana ... zoom jest niezalezny ....
A: (model) Kept as it is: the selection is chosen by hand (dragged, on the map, a lap, a block, the overview) and the zoom is independent of it: zooming with the wheel changes the range shown, not the selection. A selection made by hand still zooms to it, as asked before. (no requirement)
Q: (użytkownik) przycisk chart przeun na prawo ...
A: (model) The "Chart" button moves to the right end of the toolbar's second row, after the range shown, next to where its menu slides in. (no requirement)
Q: (użytkownik) zoom to selection i whole run ... juz chyba nie ma sensu .. wsyarrczy 1 przycisk back to whole ? i jakas ikona zamiast tekstu
A: (model) One icon button instead of "Zoom to selection" and "Whole run": arrows pointing out to the corners (named "Whole run", "Back to the whole run" on hover); it shows the whole run and clears the selection, as "Whole run" did. A selection still zooms to it when made.
Q: (użytkownik) A test or a planned workout? Find the runs with the same laps. Block from these laps - to daj pod chartem albo usun wogole
Q: (użytkownik) popup make a block from selection tak samo pod w menu po prawej stronie
A: (model) Both go into the chart menu on the right, in a section "Make a block": the block types for the selection (route segment, workout structure, effort, steady fragment), or a hint to select a stretch first, and "Block from these laps" with its sentence. The head of the statistics keeps only the selection (its minutes and seconds) and its ✕; a selection made opens no bar.
Q: (użytkownik) iformacje o selected mam 3 miejscach w tym momencie ma byc tylko nadole w widget selection
A: (model) The selection is told once, in the statistics widget at the bottom: "Selection", its clock range, its time and distance, and its ✕. The line "Selected min … · N s" next to it and the sentence about the selection in the chart menu go; the menu keeps only the block types under "Make a block".
Q: (użytkownik) usun przycisk whole run ...  ... zamknieci selelckji na dole wraca do calego treningu
A: (model) The whole-run button goes. Closing the selection with its ✕ in the statistics widget clears it and shows the whole run; with no selection the wheel zooms out to the whole run, and the key 0 on the focused chart shows it at once.
Q: (użytkownik) usun tekst kolo przycsku chart [zrzut: „7:37–26:23 of 31:30”]
A: (model) The readout of the range shown ("7:37–26:23 of 31:30") leaves the screen; it stays only for screen readers, which announce the range when it changes. The overview's window and the time axis show the range. (no requirement)
Q: (użytkownik) jesli chodzi o wykres - co radzisz dac?  linie tredu ? jakiegos spline aby odszumic ? zaznaczony min, max i linie avg?
A: (model) 1. Smoothing that follows the zoom (a spline only joins points, a mean removes noise), with Raw / Smooth in the chart menu; 2. the average as a dashed line and the min and max as points, for the metric whose scale shows, from the same data as the statistics, a statistic pointed at in the table lit on the chart; 3. a trend only in the selection, as a number (change per 10 min) with the decoupling of pace from heart rate (Pa:HR), not as lines over the whole run.
Q: (użytkownik) zrob 1,2 i 3
A: (model) 1. In Smooth (the default) each line is the rolling mean of its 10 s windows over a span of 1/30 of the range shown, from 10 s (raw) to 2 min, stops still breaking the line; Raw draws the windows as before. 2. For the metric whose scale shows, over the selection or else the range shown: a dashed line at its average and points at its min and max, each with its value, from the same 10 s windows with movement as the statistics; pointing at a Min, Avg or Max cell of the statistics lights that mark (for any metric shown). 3. With a stretch selected, the statistics add a row "Trend /10 min": the least-squares slope of each metric over the selection's windows, per 10 minutes (needs at least 1 minute); and a chip "Pa:HR" with the decoupling of the selection: the efficiency (speed per heartbeat) of its first half against its second, in %, as the decoupling of pace from heart rate is reckoned in endurance training (Friel).
Q: (użytkownik) punktu nie pokrywaja sie z wykresem: [zrzuty: punkt „max 214 W” nad linią, „min 97 W” pod nią; „min 4:25 /km” nad linią tempa]
A: (model) The points came from the raw 10 s windows while the line is smoothed (and drawn within its band's scale), so a spike of one window lay off the line. The min and max points now mark the extremes of the line as drawn (smoothed or raw, over the selection or the range shown) and give its values, so they sit on it; the statistics table keeps the raw windows, and the average line its mean.
Q: (użytkownik) nawet w surowych jest blad
A: (model) Raw draws the 10 s windows as the line shows them (the median of each window and its neighbours, the windows next to a stop left out), not the windows themselves, so a raw window's extreme could lie off the raw line too. The points mark the extremes of the line drawn in either mode, so they sit on it in Raw as in Smooth; the test checks both.
Q: (użytkownik) dodaj operacje na mapie ... zoom przesuwanie mapy automatycznie synchronizuje wykres
A: (model) The route map zooms with the mouse wheel around the point under the pointer (in fine steps, the tiles scaled between their levels) and pans by dragging; after each move the chart shows the range of time of the route seen on the map (from the first to the last moment the route is in view; the whole run when all of it is). A click without a drag still picks the ends of a stretch. Zooming or selecting on the chart still fits the map to it; a map moved by hand is not snapped back while the chart follows it.

a58faa23-2592-4664-90ca-6b1c0143af21.description: The picker of the Analysis screen, opened by "+ Add block or run", with two tabs. "Blocks and runs": a search box over one list in three groups, Your blocks (kept ones, with their kind), Suggested, found in your runs (e.g. "1.0 km northeast-bound · route passed 43 times in 43 runs; 17 meet the conditions", each with Dismiss; taking one keeps it and adds it), and Runs (date, distance, title); the arrow keys move, Enter adds. "New block": the builder, Segment (Whole runs | Laps | Fastest stretch | Steady stretch) with its length (5 min … 10 km or a number and unit; "kept for at least" for a steady stretch), In which runs (period presets and dates, workout type, shoes, title contains; more: technique cue, heart rate from, watch, laps), The segment on average (pace, heart rate, and for runs, laps and steady stretches distance and duration, each from–to), The segment at every moment (heart rate never below / above, pace always within), More (start, the fastest or every one from each run, statistic), the name written from the rule, and the live count "15 segments in 15 runs" with the newest listed; then "Use in analysis" (the rule lives in the link) or "Save and use" (kept). From a block's chip on the Analysis screen, Edit opens the block sheet: the same builder for a rule, or the name and matching tolerances (pace band, grade, steadiness, effort before, heart rate from minute, route match, start) for a block found in the runs, with Save and re-detect and Delete block.

a5a56b28-2ba1-46be-8b29-9d87439949a9.description:
The unit project (tests/unit) blocks the network in its setup (tests/support/noNetwork.ts), so a unit test that opens a connection or fetches fails; scripts/test-metrics.mjs reads the Vitest and Playwright reports and counts the tests of each kind; the unit tests' times come from a run of the unit project alone, without coverage instrumentation (npm run check runs it first), so a busy machine does not count against them. Integration tests (tests/integration) run on the author's FIT files and the versioned fixtures and are counted on their own (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026: the real-data tests are the core of the verification here, so the pack's 70% unit and 10% end-to-end became 40% and 15%).

Threshold: 0 unit tests reach the network or run over 100 ms; unit tests at least 40% and end-to-end tests at most 15% of all tests

Tool: Vitest projects (unit, integration) and scripts/test-metrics.mjs
a5a56b28-2ba1-46be-8b29-9d87439949a9.label: Unit tests stay isolated and few are end-to-end

a5a8aff6-8927-434e-bd7d-6a4a6f338bac.action: fail the check of that change before it is committed, naming the rule and the two parts involved
a5a8aff6-8927-434e-bd7d-6a4a6f338bac.label: Violations fail the build
a5a8aff6-8927-434e-bd7d-6a4a6f338bac.rationale: A violation is cheapest to fix in the pull request that brings it; after the merge others start to depend on it (Building Evolutionary Architectures, atomic fitness functions). Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026, need "Strideprism MVP specification": "Local only"): the check of a change is npm run check before it is committed; there is no pull request or merge yet.
a5a8aff6-8927-434e-bd7d-6a4a6f338bac.unwanted_condition: a change adds a dependency the rules forbid or a cycle

a68e5272-8d6d-4b4e-b4c9-69e5daeeedbe.action: compute heart rate for every instance of that block from that minute of the block to its end, the same for all its instances; without the attribute, heart rate is the mean over the whole block; show the heart rate start on the block as one of its attributes; effort and workout-type blocks start heart rate at minute 5 of the block by default
a68e5272-8d6d-4b4e-b4c9-69e5daeeedbe.feature: a block definition sets a heart rate start (minutes after the start of the block)
a68e5272-8d6d-4b4e-b4c9-69e5daeeedbe.label: Heart rate window per block
a68e5272-8d6d-4b4e-b4c9-69e5daeeedbe.rationale: The author (19 Nov 2026): heart rate measured differently is acceptable on the condition that all runs in the block are treated the same, kept as an attribute of the block; and heart rate never excludes a run on its own ("Never exclude for HR"). The model's choice: minute 5 as the default for effort and workout-type blocks, which follow a short warm-up.

a694fdc9-58ad-462b-a996-c49812b6da79.description: Browser-only application that compares blocks of runs within the same context to detect changes that watch averages do not show. No server, no database; all data stays in a folder on the runner's disk.
a694fdc9-58ad-462b-a996-c49812b6da79.label: Strideprism

a6fde2be-ed0c-4697-a89e-fbb1224474c1.description:
Playwright opens every screen of the static export with the sample data folder in Chromium and measures LCP and CLS with the web-vitals library and Total Blocking Time (the lab stand-in for INP) from long tasks (e2e/vitals.spec.ts); the library is injected by the test only and reports through the page, never over the network. scripts/js-budget.mjs sums the gzip size of every script each screen's page loads from the export. axe-core checks every screen (e2e/accessibility.spec.ts). Lighthouse CI was the pack's tool; the local Playwright run measures the same budget (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026: local only).

Threshold: for each screen: script transfer size at most 200 KB, LCP within 2500 ms, CLS at most 0.1, Total Blocking Time within 200 ms, 0 serious or critical accessibility violations

Tool: Playwright with web-vitals, scripts/js-budget.mjs, @axe-core/playwright
a6fde2be-ed0c-4697-a89e-fbb1224474c1.label: Lab budget holds
a6fde2be-ed0c-4697-a89e-fbb1224474c1.metrics:
js.route.transfer.max <= 200 KB
e2e.lcp.max <= 2500 ms
e2e.cls.max <= 0.1
e2e.tbt.max <= 200 ms
a11y.violations{impact=serious-or-critical} == 0

aaaccc51-012a-4c14-9315-82eaa46770f1.description:
The integration project's global setup (tests/support/globalSetup.ts) copies the versioned FIT fixtures from tests/fixtures into a fresh temporary data folder for each run and loads their hand-checked expected values (tests/fixtures/expected.json); a fixture without expected values, or one that is not a FIT file, fails the setup and with it the run. The fixtures are synthetic runs (scripts/make-fixtures.mjs), not the author's: their health data stays out of the repository.

Threshold: every test run starts from a fresh temporary data folder with all FIT fixtures and their expected values loaded without error
aaaccc51-012a-4c14-9315-82eaa46770f1.label: Fixtures load in every run

ae051ad4-bb7e-4998-b355-5cae616ceadd.action: show the laps as horizontal bars over the chart, each a button as wide as the lap on the chart, and when one is chosen select the lap's stretch and zoom to it, as a stretch dragged on the chart is selected, with its statistics

ae051ad4-bb7e-4998-b355-5cae616ceadd.rationale: The runner asked: "daj mozliwosc wyboru lap-a jako selekcji", then: "lapy to maja byc pokazana jako przyciski poziome paski nad wykresem, jak na niego klikne to sie zumuje ... tak jak selekcja". The model's choices: the strip follows the chart's x axis (by time or by distance) and its zoom; a bar is named by the lap's number and distance; the lap selected is marked on the strip and in the laps table; a double click on the chart inside a lap and a click on its row in the laps table select it too; the strip replaces the Lap list and the lap labels.

ae98bcc0-d501-45fc-b39d-c304e5a7b242.description: The runner's chosen folder: fit/ (FIT files, never modified), strideprism/manifest.json, user/ (gear.json, run-tags.json, block-definitions.json, never recomputed) and derived/ (runs/<id>.json, runs-index.json, segments.json, block-instances.json, day-state.json, fully rebuildable).
ae98bcc0-d501-45fc-b39d-c304e5a7b242.label: Data Folder
ae98bcc0-d501-45fc-b39d-c304e5a7b242.technology: File System Access API, columnar JSON files

aec32856-5ea5-4f0e-8316-178aff6a9838.description: People use this front end on their own devices, browsers and networks, some with disabilities and assistive technology. It has to load and respond quickly on an ordinary phone, work in the browsers its users have, be usable by everyone, look and behave consistently, and be built on a framework the team knows and that keeps receiving fixes. The choices and the numbers it is held to must be written down and checked, not rediscovered after users complain. The checks assume one front end per repository with its package.json at the root, a versions.txt listing the endoflife.date products and cycles in use, server templates (htmx) under templates/ or src/, and a RUM table rum_events(name, value, page_group, received_at) fed by the page.
aec32856-5ea5-4f0e-8316-178aff6a9838.label: A fast, accessible front end

b0289efc-ad5a-46b3-b57d-9abbb703ae9a.label: Residual pace correction

b0e29eb0-ab9e-4b68-be1e-f42e6071ba9f.description:
The heart rate trend on the promenade segment, northbound, in the 4:45–5:15/km band agrees with the result of 18 Nov 2026 where the two measure the same thing: heart rate about 135 on 14 Nov (±2 bpm taken as “about”: the model's choice), and at least 5 steady passes. Acceptance criterion 3, on the author's data.

Revised on 19 Nov 2026 (the author's decision): the preliminary analysis counted pace as distance over total time, waits at the crossings (auto-pause) included, which put August–September passes run at 4:02–4:44/km into the band (34 passes, heart rate 149–154). The application measures pace while moving and rejects a pass stopped for more than 10 s, so those passes are not steady passes and the 34 and 149–154 are no longer conditions.
b0e29eb0-ab9e-4b68-be1e-f42e6071ba9f.label: Matches preliminary analysis

b123dc6d-e4bc-46b0-b2c2-af5f46cada59.label: Steady pass accepted
b123dc6d-e4bc-46b0-b2c2-af5f46cada59.then: the Block Instance is accepted into the comparison

b1707f8d-4ee5-434c-a5c1-8545b9b1c76a.action: style the components only through the theme's design tokens (the CSS custom properties of the light and dark theme), with 0 colours set outside them
b1707f8d-4ee5-434c-a5c1-8545b9b1c76a.label: Library used through its theme
b1707f8d-4ee5-434c-a5c1-8545b9b1c76a.rationale: The application has no component library (ADR Built with React, revised 19 Nov 2026): its own components are styled through its theme, so the theme is the one place a colour changes, in both the light and the dark theme.

b277147e-4dc1-40fe-8a58-9004d82b2740.action: keep in the shared kernel only types and contracts used by at least two parts, with no dependency on a part and no third-party library beyond the allowed pure ones, at most 5% of the source lines, and changes approved by the owners of every part that uses it as the Code review and branching pack decides ownership
b277147e-4dc1-40fe-8a58-9004d82b2740.label: Shared kernel stays small
b277147e-4dc1-40fe-8a58-9004d82b2740.rationale: A shared kernel is shared on purpose and kept small; a growing "common" folder couples everything to everything (Evans, Domain-Driven Design, Shared Kernel).

b2ecee7e-c463-4adf-9bdc-167842a010a9.given: a data folder with eight short runs a week apart, pace quickening 5 s/km a week, five of them tagged easy

b2ecee7e-c463-4adf-9bdc-167842a010a9.when: two rules are computed together, the fastest 2 minutes of every run and the easy runs whole by their maximum, then the easy rule alone

b42594f3-27b1-4808-a1a2-8db3d739d2d9.description: A stretch of route found in several runs' GPS tracks: a reference track sampled every 10 m, its length and the number of runs that pass it. Derived and rebuildable.
b42594f3-27b1-4808-a1a2-8db3d739d2d9.label: Route Segment

b493eda5-2af5-4894-8ad8-5ddd03cd76ff.description: Strict matching of one candidate fragment against its Block Definition's tolerances, then its metric results.
b493eda5-2af5-4894-8ad8-5ddd03cd76ff.label: Match a Block Instance

b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.description: Speed variation (the coefficient-of-variation condition) is judged on the moving samples, and time spent standing is its own condition: samples below 0.5 m/s plus the gaps where the watch recorded nothing (auto-pause), at most 10 s. Found while comparing with the preliminary analysis of 18 Nov 2026: several August–September promenade passes held 55–110 s of auto-pause at crossings.
b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.gherkin: And a block with a stop in its last 2 minutes is accepted the same way, every metric included
b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.given: a steady 5:00/km block 10 minutes into the run, during which the watch paused for 40 s at a crossing (no samples recorded)
b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.label: Stop measured on the moving part
b4dabb76-4038-490d-b824-c77328ba52ac.then: it is accepted with pace 5:00/km and heart rate from the moving samples, and its stop of 40 s is recorded in its context

b5600968-c043-44c7-80a2-a5aa2be5d6f2.action: cover at least 80% of new and changed lines, branches included, with automated tests, measured on each check of a change
b5600968-c043-44c7-80a2-a5aa2be5d6f2.label: New code is covered
b5600968-c043-44c7-80a2-a5aa2be5d6f2.rationale: A gate on new code keeps coverage from falling without demanding that old code be fixed first (SonarQube, Clean as You Code; ISO/IEC 25010 testability). Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026, need "Strideprism MVP specification": "Local only"): the check of a change is npm run check before it is committed; there is no pull request or merge yet.

b56414c2-a1f2-48bf-b827-2da00a91bfe3.then: it is kept among the user's Block Definitions in user/block-definitions.json with origin "recommendation"

b5b4d684-1cc3-4404-b87d-575310014b5a.description: What the user says about one run: workout type, technique cue, an optional shoe override and a note; workout types and technique cues come from the user's tag dictionary. User-entered.
b5b4d684-1cc3-4404-b87d-575310014b5a.label: Run Tag

b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.action: remove the definition and its detected instances, and propose it again as a suggestion when it came from one
b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.label: Deletable block
b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.rationale: The runner asked for a way to remove blocks: "nie mam opcji usuwania blokow". The need says nothing more, so the rest is the model's choice: a confirmation first, because the deletion also removes the detected instances (it keeps Analysis and A/B free of a block that no longer exists); a block that came from a suggestion is suggested again, so a deletion by mistake is undone by accepting it again.
b719ad21-3e91-4ed0-bf3d-319783d781db.trigger: the user deletes a block definition and confirms it

b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.action: show in its statistics the trend of each metric shown as its change per 10 minutes, and the decoupling of pace from heart rate over the stretch
b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.label: Trend of a selection
b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.rationale: The runner asked: "linie tredu ?", then: "zrob 1,2 i 3". The model's choices: a trend only within a selection and as a number, not a line over the whole run, where intervals and warm-ups make a straight line misleading; the trend is the least-squares slope of the 10 s windows with movement, given per 10 minutes, for a selection of 1 minute or more; the decoupling (Pa:HR) compares the efficiency, speed per heartbeat, of the stretch's first half with its second, in % (positive: the heart rate drifted up against the pace), as it is reckoned in endurance training (Friel, The Cyclist's Training Bible / TrainingPeaks).
b77c2579-a694-46f3-b57d-9896de47072a.trigger: the runner selects a stretch of a run

b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.given: 10 s windows alternating 140 and 160 bpm, with a stop of 3 windows in the middle
b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.label: Rolling mean of a line
b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.then: the smoothed values are 150 bpm away from the stop, the stop stays a break; the span is 60 s for 30 minutes, 10 s (no smoothing) for 5 minutes, and at most 120 s
b7dbaa34-7d0f-4b7f-ba30-8780a49aeb4e.when: they are smoothed over 1 minute, and the span is reckoned for a run of 30 minutes and of 5 minutes shown

b81bafdf-940d-4c8a-a04c-0c4e29d8e9e2.given: Block Instances of "25-minute tempo" run in "Shoes A" and in "Shoes B"
b81bafdf-940d-4c8a-a04c-0c4e29d8e9e2.label: Tempo trend filtered
b81bafdf-940d-4c8a-a04c-0c4e29d8e9e2.then: only the instances run in "Shoes A" are shown over time
b81bafdf-940d-4c8a-a04c-0c4e29d8e9e2.when: the user opens its Trend for pace with the context filter shoes = "Shoes A"

b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.action: draw each line as the rolling mean of its 10 s windows over a span that grows with the range shown, keeping the breaks at stops
b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.label: Smoothing that follows the zoom
b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.precondition: the run chart is set to Smooth
b8bef40a-5e12-4451-b5e3-c5dffc6de4d2.rationale: The runner asked: "jakiegos spline aby odszumic", then: "zrob 1,2 i 3". The model's choices: a spline only joins points smoothly, a mean removes the noise; the span is 1/30 of the range shown, from 10 s (the windows as they are) up to 2 min; Smooth is the default and Raw / Smooth sits in the chart menu.

b90202ab-2fcb-414f-83ca-2f368c7e56ed.description:
Playwright runs the journeys against the static export served by a plain static file server (scripts/static-server.mjs), with no retries and forbidOnly; scripts/test-metrics.mjs reads the Playwright report and records failed and skipped tests, and npm run check exits non-zero on either. Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026): there is no merge; a change is committed after npm run check passes.

Threshold: all end-to-end tests pass before a change is committed, with 0 skipped

Tool: Playwright (JSON report) with scripts/test-metrics.mjs
b90202ab-2fcb-414f-83ca-2f368c7e56ed.label: Journeys gate the release

And its metric means and per-minute profile

bb318d07-1e0a-48d4-942c-8ecad440f7c5.then: it shows its four context layers, first the block layer: pace, grade, duration, direction and the profile of metrics

c2d112a5-91f6-4e51-946c-920566ef771e.action: offer, beside the recorded metrics, the running efficiency of every block instance, every run and every 10 s window of a run: the speed per heartbeat in metres per beat, speed in m/s × 60 / heart rate in bpm, computed from the same moving samples as the heart rate, so that it can be followed in Analysis, A/B and the run's charts like any metric
c2d112a5-91f6-4e51-946c-920566ef771e.label: Running efficiency metric
c2d112a5-91f6-4e51-946c-920566ef771e.rationale: The author's request of 19 Nov 2026: a metric for the efficiency of running, speed relative to heart rate. The model's choice: metres per heartbeat (higher is better; the 60 turns m/s into m/min, and beats are per minute), the plain speed (not grade-adjusted), the heart rate window of the block, and the run's 10 s windows for its charts.

c5829292-1066-494a-9c63-78abe795aa96.action: run the unit and integration tests within 10 minutes and fail the check on any failure
c5829292-1066-494a-9c63-78abe795aa96.label: Fast tests on every change
c5829292-1066-494a-9c63-78abe795aa96.rationale: Feedback that takes longer than about ten minutes is no longer waited for, and changes pile up untested (Fowler, Continuous Integration: keep the build fast). Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026, need "Strideprism MVP specification": "Local only"): the check of a change is npm run check before it is committed; there is no pull request or merge yet.
c5829292-1066-494a-9c63-78abe795aa96.trigger: a change is checked before it is committed

c647f82f-e4f1-4c37-b71e-08a72a967714.action: find in every run the fastest fragment of an effort block's distance or duration, on any route (a time trial run on 2 different routes is one block), and take it as an instance of that block when its pace is at least 15% faster than the rest of the run; and propose an effort block when at least 3 runs hold such an effort of 3, 5 or 10 km or of 10, 20 or 30 minutes
c647f82f-e4f1-4c37-b71e-08a72a967714.label: Effort blocks on any route
c647f82f-e4f1-4c37-b71e-08a72a967714.rationale: The author's choice (19 Nov 2026): logical blocks independent of the route, e.g. a time trial on 2 different routes. The model's choice: the 15% margin over the rest of the run (on the author's runs 8% caught every faster finish and interval set), the standard lengths 3, 5 and 10 km and 10, 20 and 30 minutes (1 km caught mostly intervals; it can still be defined from a selection), and the 3 runs.

c68701bb-cda9-41a6-a434-1fb4199752aa.description: The state of one date computed from the user's own runs: load from the previous 3 days and from the previous 7 days. Key: date. Derived.
c68701bb-cda9-41a6-a434-1fb4199752aa.label: Day State

c6b6af5b-b448-4610-b76f-9621eaef5f67.action: skip that run without creating a duplicate record
c6b6af5b-b448-4610-b76f-9621eaef5f67.label: No duplicate runs
c6b6af5b-b448-4610-b76f-9621eaef5f67.rationale: F1: the start time is the key of a Run; a repeated import adds no records.
c6b6af5b-b448-4610-b76f-9621eaef5f67.unwanted_condition: an imported FIT file holds a run whose start time equals the start time of a run already imported

c6d5b5bc-63e5-4e1d-b3e0-9f4b74617881.description: Everything on one screen, across its whole width (no scrolling at 1440 × 900 and larger). Head: title (or date), date and time, then one compact line of figures (distance, moving time, average pace, average heart rate, elevation gain), device, laps, temperature, "Add to Analysis". Over the chart a strip of laps, one horizontal bar each, a button as wide as the lap on the x axis, named "Lap N · X km" when wide enough: a click selects the lap and zooms to it. Below the head, one card: a toolbar in two rows: the metric pills to choose (up to 4 on, each with its colour swatch); then a short line of what the chart is set to (Bands or Overlaid, by time or distance, blocks drawn) and, at the right end, the "Chart" button (the range shown is announced to screen readers only); the mouse wheel over the chart zooms around the pointer. The "Chart" button slides a menu in from the right, over the map and laps and without dimming the chart: Lines "Bands / Overlaid", Line "Smooth / Raw" (the rolling mean over 1/30 of the range shown, or the 10 s windows), X axis "Time / Distance", Blocks in this run ("Draw on the chart", the list: pointing at one draws it, a click selects it), Make a block (the block types for the selection, or a hint to select first, and "Block from these laps"), Zones (which metrics shown have zones, a link to Settings); it closes with ✕, Escape or the button; a selection (dragged, on the map, a lap: list, label, double click or table row, a block) zooms the chart and the map to it at once; under it, side by side, the chart on the left and on its right the route map (the wheel zooms around the pointer, a drag pans, and the chart then shows the range of time of the route in view; click two points to select) with the run's laps under it, scrolled inside (a click on a lap selects it). The chart: the chosen metrics laid over each other, each line scaled to its own range, the focused metric's ticks at the left, laps as alternating bands, kept blocks as washed bands with names only when the toggle "Blocks" in the toolbar is on (off by default) or for the one block pointed at in the list, zones as stripes, the selection as an accent wash, a crosshair with a tooltip listing every line's value and zone at the pointer; two x axes under it, the chosen one (clock or km) and the other at the same places; the focused metric's average as a dashed line and its min and max as points with their values (from the statistics; a Min, Avg or Max cell pointed at lights its mark); a legend of the lines, each with its range, a click focuses one; an overview strip of the whole run whose window is the range shown, growing and shrinking with the zoom, the selection marked under it: dragging the window moves the range and the selection with it, dragging elsewhere selects a new stretch; the chart takes the height the screen leaves. Drag on the chart to select a stretch; pinch or Ctrl/⌘ + scroll zooms around the pointer, a sideways scroll moves. At the bottom, across the full width: the statistics of the selection (or the whole run, or the zoomed range): its time and distance, the selection told once in its head ("Selection", its clock range, time and distance) and its ✕, which clears it and shows the whole run, a Pa:HR chip (the decoupling of pace from heart rate) for a selection, and a table with a column per metric shown and min, avg and max in rows, and for a selection a row "Trend /10 min".

cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.action: reject it for every metric with the reason, so that no metric is left out of an instance on its own
cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.label: Minimum block length
cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.rationale: A fragment shorter than a minute gives no meaningful mean of any metric. One decision per run (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026, need "Strideprism MVP specification": "Never exclude for HR"): an accepted instance counts for every metric, heart rate included, computed from the block's heart rate window. The spec's per-metric minimum (4 minutes for heart rate) is dropped by that decision; the 60 s of the gait metrics becomes the block's minimum.
cdc3cba3-c6e0-4935-ae73-d3ddd6fdd564.unwanted_condition: a block instance is shorter than 60 s

cf881669-ade1-4276-8e27-b57217debcd7.action: conform to WCAG 2.2 level AA on every page, with 0 serious or critical automated accessibility violations, every function operable by keyboard alone, and a manual audit with a screen reader before each major release
cf881669-ade1-4276-8e27-b57217debcd7.label: Accessible to WCAG 2.2 AA
cf881669-ade1-4276-8e27-b57217debcd7.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA is the level EN 301 549, the European Accessibility Act and most public-sector rules require; automated checks find only part of the failures, hence the keyboard journey and the manual audit (W3C WCAG 2.2; EN 301 549).

d00107b1-a4df-4790-b933-7c13969f8952.rationale: The runner's remodelling: "4.2 system wybiera mi wszystkie segmenty i je uzywa", and the earlier form of an answer, "tabela wyników z linkami do biegów" with "ranking kolejnych". Showing what was left out and why keeps the result transparent, as for every block (requirement "Result transparency").

d3c81008-1d9a-459b-b77c-ba4b66820d00.rationale: Front-end frameworks support a major for a limited time (Angular 18 months, Node.js-based tooling with its runtime); after that, security fixes stop (endoflife.date).

d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.alternatives:
1. A frozen baseline with a ratchet: adoptable today on an old codebase, at the cost of carrying known violations.
2. Warnings only: visible, and ignored within weeks.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.consequences:
• A violation never reaches main, so nobody comes to depend on one.
• Switching the check on needs a clean codebase first; on an old one that is a project of its own.
• A rule that turns out wrong blocks everyone until it is changed, which keeps the rules honest.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.context: The code in this element is cut into parts (modules, packages, libraries) and keeps changing. Without written and checked rules, every shortcut adds a dependency nobody decided on: one module reads another's internals, two packages import each other, and a "common" folder grows until every change touches everything. The forces: rules kept only in a wiki erode within months; a cycle makes two parts one, so neither can be tested, owned or released alone; sharing code saves typing but couples the teams that share it; a boundary nobody owns is crossed by whoever is in a hurry; and an old codebase cannot fix every violation at once. What the parts are (layers, rings, slices) is the Architecture style pack; who owns each part is the Code review and branching pack; this pack keeps the boundaries between the parts.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.decision: The dependency check (scripts/boundaries.mjs) runs in every check of a change (npm run check) and in the unit tests, and any violation fails it: there is no baseline and no exception list. Existing violations were fixed before the check was switched on (19 Nov 2026: the cycles between ingest, prepare, blocks and context were broken by the shared kernel and the pipeline part). Local only for now: a change is committed after npm run check passes.
d80d0ec6-3ee4-4a8d-b084-2724d2b1e34b.label: Every violation fails the build

da832a20-4c6e-48e6-9bce-d34a6396158a.label: Only declared dependencies
da832a20-4c6e-48e6-9bce-d34a6396158a.rationale: Declaring each dependency makes it a decision visible in review; rules that are not checked erode with every shortcut (Building Evolutionary Architectures, ch. 2; Spring Modulith, allowed dependencies).

db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.alternatives:
1. A testing trophy: mostly integration tests, better for glue code, slower feedback.
2. An ice-cream cone of manual and end-to-end tests: slow, brittle and late; the shape to move away from.
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.consequences:
• Fast, precise feedback: a failing unit test names the rule that broke.
• Refactoring that changes internal interfaces rewrites many unit tests; test behaviour, not methods, to limit it.
• Wiring bugs (configuration, queries, serialisation) are caught only by the thinner integration layer.
• Requires code where the logic can be called without infrastructure.
• The gate costs build time in proportion to what it proves: coverage is free, a mutation score adds minutes.
• Where the end-to-end tests run decides what they can stop: before the merge, before production, or only after.
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.context: Code lives in this element and changes every week; the tests decide whether a change can be released with confidence or only with hope. The forces: fast tests give feedback in minutes but exercise little of the wiring, while end-to-end tests exercise everything but are slow, brittle and late; coverage shows what was run, not what was checked; tests that share data or depend on order fail at random, and a suite that fails at random is soon ignored; copies of production data make realistic tests but carry personal data; and a test that fails only sometimes teaches everyone to rerun until green. Contract tests between the system's parts and with outside callers are decided in the Communication style and API evolution packs.
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.decision: Tests follow the pyramid, adapted to real data: unit tests of the domain logic under tests/unit run with Vitest on synthetic data, without network access, in under 100 ms each, at least 40% of all tests; integration tests under tests/integration run the processing pipeline against a temporary data folder with the versioned synthetic FIT fixtures (tests/fixtures) and the author's FIT files (test_data, kept out of the repository); a few end-to-end tests, at most 15%, cover import, block-definition, trend, ab-comparison (Playwright, Chromium) against the static export. Every check of a change (npm run check) runs unit and integration tests within 10 minutes, in random order. Gate: coverage of new code, 80%; mutation testing with Stryker is deferred. Flaky tests: quarantine (quarantine.json, nightly run), then a fix or deletion. Local only for now (the author's decision of 19 Nov 2026).
db7bc61d-5dad-4fc7-a241-5d1fa31ca854.label: A test pyramid

e52ebeb4-a468-47dd-8fb2-2983ba904533.given: best stretches that follow Riegel's law with the exponent 1.07, 4:00/km at 10 minutes, from 3 to 60 minutes, a 60-second sprint, and then an easy 2-hour run far below the law
e52ebeb4-a468-47dd-8fb2-2983ba904533.label: Estimate fitted to the bests
e52ebeb4-a468-47dd-8fb2-2983ba904533.then: the exponent 1.07 is recovered from the six bests of 3 minutes and more (the sprint left out), the estimated pace at 10 minutes is 4:00, the predicted 10 km is about 44 minutes and the marathon about 3 h 29 min along the law, the critical speed comes from the four bests of 2–20 minutes with a positive D'; with the easy run the slope steepens but the line still passes through a strongest best and no best lies above it; two bests give no estimate and bests of 30 minutes and more alone give no critical speed

e54a7ba9-36d5-4dfe-84b8-a3cf912726b9.description: Matching rules (also used by detection), instance selection, counting each fragment once, series per sensor, noise threshold, trend and A/B results with verdict, confounding warning and minimum counts.

ee3092a3-e0ec-4a29-9eeb-df3fe3663fb3.quote: People use this front end on their own devices, browsers and networks, some with disabilities and assistive technology. It has to load and respond quickly on an ordinary phone, work in the browsers its users have, be usable by everyone, look and behave consistently, and be built on a framework the team knows and that keeps receiving fixes. The choices and the numbers it is held to must be written down and checked, not rediscovered after users complain. The checks assume one front end per repository with its package.json at the root, a versions.txt listing the endoflife.date products and cycles in use, server templates (htmx) under templates/ or src/, and a RUM table rum_events(name, value, page_group, received_at) fed by the page.

ef4fb321-3d4b-495d-bcb5-7212a4433066.quote: The code in this element must stay easy to understand, test and change as it grows and as people come and go. That needs parts with clear boundaries: a change to one part should not ripple through the others, each part should be testable on its own, and the rules about what may depend on what should hold because the build checks them, not because everyone remembers them. The checks below share one layout: each part lives in src/modules/<name> with its published API in src/modules/<name>/index.ts and its declarations in src/modules/<name>/module.json; shared code, where allowed, lives in src/shared-kernel; the rules are in .dependency-cruiser.cjs and run as `npm run check:deps` (depcruise src --config .dependency-cruiser.cjs); known violations, where frozen, are in .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json.
